item.title: Aday Mara could see NBA debut delayed as old Spanish club threaten Thunder
item.description: As excited as the Oklahoma City Thunder have been about Aday Mara, they're experiencing their first bump on the road. His former Spanish club — Basket Zaragoza — is threatening to take legal action if he suits up for Opening Night and beyond. The team claims he remains under contract with them through the 2026-27 season. Oh wow. That's significant. At least, on paper, it is. Basket Zaragoza has been in contact with the Thunder, NBA and FIBA over the contract dispute. The Spanish club also stated it's prepared to take any necessary legal actions required to ensure he doesn't suit up for OKC. Meanwhile, the Thunder released an official statement in response. Per NBA insider Marc Stein : "Aday last played three years of NCAA college basketball and therefore, as advised by the NBA, no clearance from the Spanish team is required for him to play in the NBA." Mara played with Basket Zaragoza from 2021-23. He then enrolled at UCLA and played two collegiate seasons there from 2023-25. Afterward, he transferred to Michigan for the past collegiate season. That's where he broke out as the eventual No. 12 pick of the 2026 NBA draft. I guess we'll see if anything materializes over this dispute. If I had to guess, I think the Thunder find a way to settle this with Mara's old team. Whether that's ignoring their threats or reaching out for a conclusion. The 21-year-old had a stellar preseason. He's too important to sit out over a small legal dispute like this. This article originally appeared on OKC Thunder Wire: Aday Mara could see NBA debut delayed as old Spanish club threaten Thunder

item.title: Daniel Dubois vs. Fabio Wardley 2 preview and predictions: Is revenge on the menu in Fight of the Year rematch?
item.description: Just 160 days after their instant classic in May , Daniel Dubois and Fabio Wardley are preparing to do it all over again. Their first meeting for the WBO heavyweight title in Manchester was a brutal firefight. Dubois climbed off the canvas in Rounds 1 and 3, survived an early onslaught, and turned what at times looked like an unwinnable fight into an 11th-round stoppage victory. As Dubois grew into the fight, Wardley faded out of it. The ex-champion's early success gave way to a sustained beating, with calls for his corner to throw in the towel growing louder as the punishment mounted. Eventually, referee Howard Foster intervened in the penultimate round — a compassionate call that perhaps should've been made several rounds prior. Although it is common for boxers to take as much as a year out of the ring to recover from such a taxing fight — or just after any fight in 2026 — Dubois and Wardley will run it back just over five months after their first meeting . With little more than 24 hours until their rematch at London's O2 Arena, Uncrowned examines the biggest talking points surrounding the sequel, starting with one that scarcely needs asking: Just how big are Wardley's balls? Daniel Dubois (left) and Fabio Wardley's first meeting is a frontrunner for Fight of the Year. Adam Davy - PA Images via Getty Images Daniel Dubois vs. Fabio Wardley: WBO heavyweight title Wardley's toughness cannot be questioned after his fight with Dubois. The Ipswich fighter sustained plenty of punishment late in that bout but refused to give up, adamant that he could still turn things around — as he’d done previously in his two prior fights against Joseph Parker and Justis Huni. But how many times can you go back to the well before there's nothing left? For a man with just 22 fights, Wardley has already had a physically demanding career. The wear and tear will be visible on Saturday when Dubois gets his jab going on Wardley's nose, and it busts open again. With just 160 days to heal from such a brutal affair, it’s difficult to imagine Wardley has fully recovered going into the second meeting, nor will he be able to sustain the same amount of punishment. item.dc:creator: Darshan Desai
item.content:encoded: Just 160 days after their instant classic in May , Daniel Dubois and Fabio Wardley are preparing to do it all over again. Their first meeting for the WBO heavyweight title in Manchester was a brutal firefight. Dubois climbed off the canvas in Rounds 1 and 3, survived an early onslaught, and turned what at times looked like an unwinnable fight into an 11th-round stoppage victory. As Dubois grew into the fight, Wardley faded out of it. The ex-champion's early success gave way to a sustained beating, with calls for his corner to throw in the towel growing louder as the punishment mounted. Eventually, referee Howard Foster intervened in the penultimate round — a compassionate call that perhaps should've been made several rounds prior. Although it is common for boxers to take as much as a year out of the ring to recover from such a taxing fight — or just after any fight in 2026 — Dubois and Wardley will run it back just over five months after their first meeting . With little more than 24 hours until their rematch at London's O2 Arena, Uncrowned examines the biggest talking points surrounding the sequel, starting with one that scarcely needs asking: Just how big are Wardley's balls? Daniel Dubois (left) and Fabio Wardley's first meeting is a frontrunner for Fight of the Year. Adam Davy - PA Images via Getty Images Daniel Dubois vs. Fabio Wardley: WBO heavyweight title Wardley's toughness cannot be questioned after his fight with Dubois. The Ipswich fighter sustained plenty of punishment late in that bout but refused to give up, adamant that he could still turn things around — as he’d done previously in his two prior fights against Joseph Parker and Justis Huni. But how many times can you go back to the well before there's nothing left? For a man with just 22 fights, Wardley has already had a physically demanding career. The wear and tear will be visible on Saturday when Dubois gets his jab going on Wardley's nose, and it busts open again. With just 160 days to heal from such a brutal affair, it’s difficult to imagine Wardley has fully recovered going into the second meeting, nor will he be able to sustain the same amount of punishment. The rematch has likely come too soon for him to be at his best. Wardley is his most dangerous early — and that surely has to be the game plan. Wardley had Dubois down just seconds into their first fight and then put him on the floor again in Round 3. The former champion must believe that if he can jump on Dubois in the opening few rounds and make it a shootout, with his speed advantage and raw power, he has the chance to end things quickly. Dubois was floored both times by overhand rights near the side of his head, which crumbled his balance and saw his legs betray him momentarily. The overhand right is very much Wardley's money punch, and with so much of Dubois' game dictated by his jab, Wardley surely will have plenty of opportunities to land that shot over Dubois' left. That strategy may also put him in harm's way, though. Dubois has ended 22 of his 23 wins inside the distance. He’s a monstrous puncher as well, and if Wardley commits to power shots early, it could leave him open to ferocious counters. In their first fight, Dubois was able to hurt Wardley, but Wardley stood up to the power better. When Dubois was caught by a big shot, he found himself on the canvas; Wardley, however, did not. But will it be the same in the rematch? Has the cumulative punishment had a lasting impact on Wardley's chin, which has been so reliable in the past? There are some comparisons between this rematch and Joe Joyce vs. Zhilei Zhang 2 in 2023. Joyce was the most durable fighter in the division. He had a granite chin and was marketed as an immovable object. Zhang was a devastating puncher, and in their first fight, Joyce stood up to his power until eye damage forced the fight to end prematurely. When they fought the second time, though, Joyce's chin wasn't the same. Zhang forced an early finish with a mammoth right hook. Another similarity to Dubois vs. Wardley 2 was the short turnaround — just five months on both occasions. Joyce was never the same fighter after the first Zhang fight, and I fear that may be the case for Wardley too. As for Dubois, the key for him in this fight will be to stay alert early and settle into a rhythm. Once Dubois can establish himself in the fight and have success with his jab, it will pave the way for him to land his heavier punches on Wardley. The champion needs to weather what will likely be a heavy storm in the opening rounds and try to take over as the fight plays out. Another key advantage in the rematch — just as it was in the first fight — is Dubois' fundamentals, which are much better than those of Wardley. Dubois was a top amateur with numerous youth and junior bouts, while Wardley came up through the white-collar route. Dubois' schooling has led him to be better prepared for the world level of the heavyweight division. It's likely Wardley is not as durable as he was in the first fight, and therefore I see Dubois breaking him down and getting him out earlier this time. item.title: Three In-House Options That Could Save the Bills’ Defense
item.description: If not for Greg Rousseau ’s blocked field goal , the conversation about the Bills’ Week 5 win looks very different. Buffalo rolls out an offense that’s tied for the league lead with 32.8 points per game. On the other hand, the defense has been terrible, allowing 28.2 points per game, which ranks fifth-worst in the NFL. Besides the defensive line holding their own, there aren’t many positives to take away so far. While things have been tough for Buffalo on defense, there is good news. They have a few options in-house that could make big differences the rest of the season. With a mix of both veterans and rookies, it leaves an interesting discussion to be had. Jalon Kilgore Has the Size and Versatility the Secondary Needs Jalon Kilgore, a fifth-round pick this past draft, was immediately met with a lot of intrigue from Bills fans. He was drafted to fill a position where Buffalo lacked depth. Outside of Cole Bishop and C.J. Gardner-Johnson , the options at safety still don’t look great. The Bills’ secondary as a whole has struggled so far this season, which is where Kilgore can help. The South Carolina product brings versatility the defense is missing after Taron Johnson was traded to the Raiders. While Kilgore’s main position is safety, he excels at playing all over the field. Whether he’s at safety or filling in at nickel corner for an injured Dee Alford , he should play. What capacity he plays in isn’t the issue; it’s the fact that he needs to be on the field. With injuries piling up in the secondary, now is the best time for the Bills to see what they have with Kilgore. If they can find a way to have him play a “big nickel” role (or a third safety in a 4-2-5 scheme), there’s no doubt that he can make a difference. At 6-foot-1 and 210 pounds, he has the size to play anywhere effectively. Coverage skills will come with time, but in the big nickel role, he can use his size in the box. He’s not afraid to step up in run support and make a play, something he showed regularly at South Carolina . At this point, Buffalo’s defense has been so bad that they have nothing to lose by playing Kilgore. The team can only run practice squad players out there over him for so long. There’s no reason Kilgore shouldn’t at least get a look. He’s a talented football player, so his chance should come sooner rather than later. Jalen Kilgore is one of the most underrated DBs in this draft. At 6’1”, 211 with a 4.40, this PBU against Alabama shows exactly why. Schum (@Gridiron_Dre) March 30, 2026 Kaleb Elarms-Orr Deserves Snaps Over Dorian Williams in Coverage Kaleb Elarms-Orr is another rookie from the Bills’ 2026 draft class. The former Cal and TCU linebacker was selected in the fourth round. During the preseason, he gained a lot of attention and even made a push to start opposite Terrel Bernard . Ultimately, the other starting linebacker ended up being Dorian Williams , but Elarms-Orr has still seen some playing time. After three-plus years, Williams is who he is. He has always played well in run defense, but struggles in coverage. It’s at the point where it can’t get any worse. The argument to play Elarms-Orr over Williams is similar to the argument for Jalon Kilgore. The only way from here is up. Even if Elarms-Orr finds the field on pass coverage snaps, it could make a significant difference for the defense. While it’s easy to blame players for the defensive mishaps, some blame needs to fall on the coaching staff too. After five weeks, Joe Brady and Jim Leonhard should have a better idea of their players’ strengths and weaknesses. Just because a player starts for the defense doesn’t mean they have to play every snap. A situation like the Bills are in now could call for a rotation of players at the linebacker position. This could put Elarms-Orr and Williams in better positions to succeed. Clearly, something needs to change, and this would be the easiest in-house solution. Bernard and Elarms-Orr coming downhill pic.twitter.com/rNXWDPw7O4 — Cover 1 (@Cover1) October 8, 2026 Shaq Thompson Was Starting Playoff Games Last Year and Can’t Get a Call-Up Another interesting option the Bills have in-house to solve their defensive woes is Shaq Thompson . The former Carolina Panther played 12 games and started in six for Buffalo last season. His play might not have been at the level it used to be, but he stabilized a struggling defense. After going the entire offseason without signing elsewhere, the team decided to bring him back on the practice squad. Thompson has been sitting there all season, waiting for another opportunity to crack the roster. Brandon Beane and Joe Brady know what they’re getting with Thompson, which makes his absence more confusing. If the team doesn’t want to play rookies like Kilgore or Elarms-Orr, that’s understandable. The problem is, at this point, what do Bernard and Williams offer the defense that Thompson can’t? Thompson was starting playoff games for the team last year, and now he can’t even get a game-day call-up. This is the perfect in-house solution for the Bills if they want to add a veteran presence to the defense. It also gives the rookie options an opportunity to sit a little bit longer and develop. Many have tried to give the defense the benefit of the doubt, but time is running out. Changes need to be made. The reality for the team is that they don’t have the cap space to make a big move. They’re going to have to find something from within, and Shaq Thompson could be that. Laser focus by Shaq Thompson to knock it out NEvsBUF on NBC Stream on @NFLPlus + Peacock pic.twitter.com/E79AWEmMBl — NFL (@NFL) October 6, 2025 The Bills Don’t Have the Cap Space to Buy a Fix Buffalo has $4.7 million in cap space. That’s not nearly enough for a significant trade deadline acquisition. If they’re going to make a move, it has to be for someone on a cheap deal. At that point, their best bet is to look for the solutions internally first. Between Jalon Kilgore, Kaleb Elarms-Orr, and Shaq Thompson, they have options. These players allow them to make changes to the struggling secondary and linebacker corps. The one thing the team has on their side right now is time. With the trade deadline approaching after Week 9 , they can make some internal changes. If they don’t work out, then they can pivot to someone on the trade market. The team can’t sit on their hands and continue to watch a bad defense. Even with a quarterback like Josh Allen , it’s not every year that they lead the league in points per game. The sense of urgency should start right now for the Bills. Changes need to be made before it’s too late. The post Three In-House Options That Could Save the Bills’ Defense appeared first on The Lead .

item.title: Match Preview: Dortmund Back in League Play as They Travel to Union Berlin
item.description: Borussia Dortmund are back in Bundesliga action as they travel to Berlin on Saturday. It’s been a rough week-long stretch for Die Schwarzgelben. First, squandering a two goal lead to Werder Bremen in the Bundesliga last week, followed by a grueling mid-week Champions League defeat in Norway at the hands of Bodø/Glimt. Needless to say, BVB will look to get back on track, sitting in second place in the league due to goal differential with Freiburg. Union Berlin on the other hand have had a torrid start to the season, sitting at 16th in the league. They’ve allowed the second most goals (17) in the league so far this campaign. They did however pick up three points last week after their first win in this year’s Bundesliga campaign, with a 1-0 victory over Elversberg. Momentum for Union Berlin, perhaps? Borussia Dortmund will look to put an end to any glimmer of that. And in the process potentially match a club record 16 points out of a possible 18 after six games (most recently during the 2017/2018 season). Player to Watch: Julian Ryerson The Norwegian missed last week’s clash against Werder Bremen due to a rib injury sustained over international break. He came on in the 60th minute for BVB’s champion’s league clash – in Ryerson’s home country. Now he’ll be closer to full strength, with something to prove against his former side, where he played for over four years. He provides that much needed box-to-box edge from the wing that could impact the game on multiple levels. Plus Nico Schlotterbeck was rested for the midweek European fixture. With him returning, that should solidify the backline more given Ryerson license to make his marauding runs. Niko Kovač’s side can’t afford another slow start. Ryerson provides that burst of energy from the get-go to feed Serhou Guirassy, early and often. Predicted Lineup Score Prediction Union Berlin will be the scrappy homeside and keep this tight for a majority of the match. But I expect Dortmund’s attacking quality to shine through, especially Guirassy. The striker has has an impressive track record against the capital club, with eight goals in eight appearances . Dortmund 3-1 Union Berlin. Your Thoughts? What are your predictions for Saturday’s Bundesliga clash? Will Dortmund right the ship and get back to their winning ways? Let us know in the comments below!

item.title: Lamar Jackson injury: Ravens QB ‘likely’ out vs. Browns
item.description: Photo by Rich von Biberstein/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Baltimore Ravens are “likely” to be without star quarterback Lamar Jackson for the second consecutive week. Jackson, who sprained his left ankle in Baltimore’s win over the Tennessee Titans back on October 4, was not available for the media portion of practice on Friday ahead of the Ravens’ game against the Cleveland Browns this weekend. Jackson has not practiced yet this week, which is a sign that Tyler Huntley is in line to start his second game in a row: Ravens QB Lamar Jackson is not present during media viewing portion of Friday’s practice, which indicates Tyler Huntley will likely start for the second straight week. Jackson missed every practice this week and hasn’t suited up since spraining his left ankle in a win over the… — Jamison Hensley (@jamisonhensley) October 16, 2026 Huntley completed 8-of-9 passes for 63 yards in relief of Jackson in the early October game against the Titans, helping Baltimore salt away a 24-18 victory. Huntley got the start for the Ravens against the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday night, completing 24-of-32 passes for 201 yards and a pair of touchdowns, as the Ravens won 30-23 in overtime. Huntley also started a late-season game against the Green Bay Packers a year ago, guiding Baltimore to a 41-24 victory in Lambeau Field. As noted by Ravens beat reporter Jamison Hensley above, in his last three starts for the Ravens — all wins — Huntley and the offense have averaged over 33 points. Our own Doug Farrar also named Huntley one of his “ AFC Secret Superstars ” after his performance against the Falcons.

item.title: Father escapes jail after 3-yr-old son falls to death in Cyprus hotel
item.description: A Cyprus court on Friday ordered a British father to pay a fine but spared him prison after he pleaded guilty to causing the death of his three-year-old son, who fell from a hotel window. Joshua Foster’s parents and other relatives were in court for the sentencing, with some weeping and embracing him after the decision was announced, according to Cypriot state media. The incident occurred in the holiday town of Paphos in July on the family’s first day on vacation. The court heard that Foster and other family members had spent time around the hotel pool before returning to their rooms to prepare for dinner. He then left the room with his son and the child’s grandfather. While they waited for the lift, he placed the child on a windowsill so that he could see a nearby water park, not realising that the window was open. The boy fell approximately 10 metres (33 feet) from the fourth floor. Despite efforts to resuscitate him, the child was pronounced dead at the local hospital. In its decision, the Paphos District Court described the incident as a “momentary error” rather than a deliberate act. Foster’s lawyer had asked the court to consider his guilty plea to the charge of causing death through a reckless, rash or dangerous act, as well as his clean criminal record and immeasurable personal loss. Speaking to reporters after the decision, defender Alexandros Alexandrou said that the “court accepted this was a momentary mistake, not conscious negligence”, arguing the case never should have gone to court. “This was an unfortunate incident. Any sentence cannot bring justice,” he added. The court imposed a 3,000 euro ($3,370) fine rather than a prison sentence. The offence carried a maximum term of four years. The 37-year-old had been allowed to return to the UK during the proceedings to attend his son’s funeral. The BBC reported that he was from Essex, near London. Vanguard News The post Father escapes jail after 3-yr-old son falls to death in Cyprus hotel appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Tommy Tant Memorial Surf Classic returns to Flagler Beach Oct. 23-25
item.description: The Tommy Tant Memorial Surf Classic returns to Flagler Beach Oct. 23–25, bringing three days of competition, a memorial paddle-out and fundraising for local students and surfers. The 24th annual event will take place just south of the Flagler Beach Pier, with 19 divisions for surfers of all ages and skill levels, according to organizers. The Tommy Tant Memorial Surf Classic returns to Flagler Beach Oct. 23–25, bringing three days of competition, a memorial paddle-out and fundraising for local students and surfers. The 24th annual event will take place just south of the Flagler Beach Pier, with 19 divisions for surfers of all ages and skill levels, according to organizers. The contest began in 1999 in memory of local surfer Tommy Tant, who died unexpectedly the previous year at age 24. Surfing supports scholarships Organizers said the event has raised more than $200,000 for the community over the years. Its current efforts support student scholarships and a Fellows Program that provides grants to help local professional surfers advance their careers. A new exhibition Saturday afternoon will feature professional surfers using a Jet Ski tow to gain speed and launch aerial maneuvers. “My brother was a big supporter of my career, so it’s exciting to watch our Fellows Program grow into its second year and to celebrate it with two of our Fellows in the Tow-At session,” said event director Will Tant, Tommy’s younger brother. Weekend schedule Competition begins Friday, Oct. 23, and continues through Sunday, Oct. 25. A kickoff party is scheduled for 7 p.m. Friday at Craeft Surf Studio, across from the contest site. It will feature live and silent auctions and an acoustic performance by Timing Belt. Other activities include raffles, live painting and a memorial paddle-out scheduled for midday Sunday. An awards ceremony will follow Sunday evening at Craeft Surf Studio, which organizers describe as the event’s new permanent home. AdventHealth physicians will also be on-site to help athletes stretch and prepare between heats. Contest registration, scholarship and volunteer applications, and additional details are available at TommyTant.com . Click here to download our free news, weather and smart TV apps. And click here to stream Channel 9 Eyewitness News live.

item.title: ‘That’s Just Motivation’ — Jaguars WR Parker Washington Opens Up on Receiving Compliment From NFL Legend Tom Brady
item.description: ‘That’s Just Motivation’ — Jaguars WR Parker Washington Opens Up on Receiving Compliment From NFL Legend Tom Brady Parker Washington has 352 receiving yards and four touchdowns through five games of the Jacksonville Jaguars’ 4-1 start, and his two-touchdown afternoon against the Philadelphia Eagles in London drew praise this week from Tom Brady, a fellow sixth-round pick who went on to win a record seven Super Bowl titles. What Tom Brady Saw in Parker Washington Brady’s comments came in the latest edition of his NFL power rankings for Fox Sports, where he kept the Jaguars at No. 5. He said Washington is no longer just a fun story but a true competitor, and he pointed to the sixth round as the place teams look when they need talent. That round is what links them: New England took Brady 199th overall in 2000, and Jacksonville picked Washington out of Penn State at No. 185 in 2023. Washington earned the mention in the 19-17 win on Oct. 11 at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. He caught six of his nine targets for 124 yards, and both of Trevor Lawrence’s touchdown passes went to him. His 51-yard catch opened the scoring in the first quarter, and his 27-yarder with 3:20 left put Jacksonville ahead 16-14. PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor Jake Elliott’s field goal gave the Eagles a 17-16 lead with eight seconds remaining, and Cam Little won it with a 57-yard field goal as time expired. Brady also credited the Jacksonville defense, which held the Eagles to 22 rushing yards. Washington didn’t hold back about what the compliment meant to him: “That means everything, you know, get recognition from one of the greats. I mean, it’s true, one of the best, you know, so really great quarterback. You know, that’s just motivation to just keep going.” “Special players in that round, you know, so let’s keep it going,” Washington said about being a sixth-round pick, same as Brady. Washington’s next test comes on Sunday, when the Jaguars, first in the AFC South, face the Houston Texans at Wembley Stadium in London. BE THE GM OF YOUR FAVORITE TEAM: PFN’s Free NFL Mock Draft Simulator The 24-year-old wideout set career highs in 2025 with 58 catches for 847 yards and five touchdowns, and he returned two punts for scores. Five games into this season, Washington’s receiving yards rank 14th in the NFL, and his touchdown catches are tied for fourth. Washington is currently ranked 12th on PFN’s WR Impact Metric with a grade of 82.7. Last season, he ranked 25th with a grade of 77.3. Jaguars general manager James Gladstone said in early September that the team was open to continuing extension talks with Washington during the season. But with Washington’s value rising, he may have more incentive to wait until the offseason, when his performance could put him in a position to seek a deal closer to the upper tier of the wide receiver market. This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network .

item.title: Troops kill two Lakurawa terrorists, recover four AK-47 rifles in Sokoto
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi Troops of Operation Fansan Yamma have neutralised two suspected Lakurawa terrorists and recovered four AK-47 rifles, eight motorcycles and other items during clearance operations in Sokoto State. The operations were conducted on October 15, 2026, as part of sustained efforts to dismantle terrorist networks and restore security in the joint operations area. The Media Information Officer of Operation Fansan Yamma, Lt. Col. Aliyu Danja, disclosed this in a statement on Friday. Danja said troops of Sector 2 first made contact with the terrorists at Waria Forest, where they engaged them in a firefight, neutralising one and recovering two AK-47 rifles, two motorcycles and other items. He said the troops subsequently engaged another group of terrorists at Sarma village, neutralising one suspect and forcing the others to flee, abandoning their equipment. According to him, further exploitation of the area led to the recovery of six additional motorcycles, two AK-47 rifles, four magazines, 23 rounds of ammunition, one communication device and other items. The operation brings the total number of terrorists neutralised to two, while the recovered weapons and equipment are expected to support ongoing efforts to disrupt the activities of armed groups in the area. Danja said the successes demonstrated the troops’ sustained commitment to dismantling terrorist networks and restoring lasting peace and security across the joint operations area. He added that the Theatre Command appreciated the continued support and cooperation of members of the public. The military urged residents to remain vigilant and promptly report suspicious activities to the nearest security outpost. The post Troops kill two Lakurawa terrorists, recover four AK-47 rifles in Sokoto appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Aston Villa’s interim boss Sørensen to remain in role for the season
item.description: Aston Villa’s interim boss Sørensen to remain in role for the season Aston Villa have announced the news that Brian Sørensen will remain in his position of interim head coach for the whole of the 2026/2027 season. The Villans revealed the news in an official club statement earlier today. The 46-year-old stepped up from his usual role of women’s technical advisor into the interim head coach role following former boss Natalia Arroyo’s departure at the end of last month. Aston Villa opted for a managerial change following a difficult start to the season. Since taking up his interim position, Sørensen has guided Aston Villa to a 3-1 victory over Newcastle United in the Subway Players Cup along with a 1-1 home draw with Crystal Palace in the Barclays Women’s Super League. The Dane will now be tasked with helping The Villans climb the Barclays Women’s Super League table. Aston Villa face a gruelling nine-match window before the next international break at the end of November. They will face six opponents in the Barclays Women’s Super League, along with three games in the Subway Players Cup. Two of the nine games are against Second City rivals Birmingham City. Aston Villa resume Barclays Women’s Super League action on Sunday afternoon when they play host to Liverpool at Keys Park in Hednesford.

Since taking up his interim position, Sørensen has guided Aston Villa to a 3-1 victory over Newcastle United in the Subway Players Cup along with a 1-1 home draw with Crystal Palace in the Barclays Women’s Super League. The Dane will now be tasked with helping The Villans climb the Barclays Women’s Super League table. Aston Villa face a gruelling nine-match window before the next international break at the end of November. They will face six opponents in the Barclays Women’s Super League, along with three games in the Subway Players Cup. Two of the nine games are against Second City rivals Birmingham City. Aston Villa resume Barclays Women’s Super League action on Sunday afternoon when they play host to Liverpool at Keys Park in Hednesford.

item.title: Braves add Brett Wisely to 40-man roster and outright DaShawn Keirsey Jr.
item.description: TAMPA, FLORIDA - FEBRUARY 26: Brett Wisely #0 of the Atlanta Braves hits a single in the fifth inning against the New York Yankees during a Grapefruit League spring training game at George M. Steinbrenner Field on February 26, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Julio Aguilar/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Atlanta Braves have been making some small and quiet moves with their roster since their elimination in the NLDS and here’s another one. After they selected Danny Young’s contract last week, the Braves have decided to do the same with Brett Wisely as well. DaShawn Keirsey Jr. ended up getting outrighted to Triple-A Gwinnett as a corresponding move so they made a decision on him at some point without publicizing it. All of this was found on the Braves’ transaction page and was reported initially by Harrison Smajovits of Atlanta Braves on SI. More #Braves activity – Brett Wisely was selected to the MLB roster – DaShawn Keirsey Jr. was outrighted to Triple-A – Luke Williams elected free agency after being outrighted to Triple-A — Harrison Smajovits (@HarrisonSmaj) October 15, 2026 Wisely didn’t make any appearances with the Braves at the big league level in 2026 as he ended up playing 125 games for the Gwinnett Stripers this season. He had himself a pretty solid year at the plate, as he hit .281/.399/.436 with 11 home runs and 127 wRC+ at the Triple-A level last season. That’s to say that I’d imagine that the Braves aren’t bringing him up at this point in the offseason because they figure that he’s part of their big league plans for 2027. Wisely has never really been able to translate his Triple-A success to big league success, so I’m guessing that the Braves figure that this is a good way to make sure that they’ll keep their options open with him being used in another transaction down the road, since putting the veteran on the 40-man roster means that he won’t be able to use his rights as a minor league vet to elect free agency. Wisely’s last stint with the big league Braves lasted all of 4 games and nine plate appearances in 2025, in case you’re wondering whether or not there’s really something here. Either way, it’s a totally procedural move that gives the Braves a chance to do something with Wisely from a transactional standpoint going forward during the offseason without potentially losing him for completely nothing. We’ll see how it goes, though.

Fulham fans fretting about life under Álvaro Arbeloa will not feel any better when they remember how things were under Marco Silva, who was one of the most effective managers in the Premier League when it came to making substitutions. Silva’s substitutes were involved in the fourth-highest goal contributions last season and the most in the 2024-25 season. Fulham knew how to dig in and salvage unlikely points. But Silva left last summer, joining Benfica after concluding he could achieve nothing more at Craven Cottage, and his replacement is already under pressure after some puzzling tactical choices. item.title: John Lynch says George Kittle asked him if the 49ers were trading for a pass rusher
item.description: Photo by Michael Zagaris/San Francisco 49ers/Getty Images) | Getty Images San Francisco 49ers general manager John Lynch was asked if trade talks around the league are increasing and whether there are more calls in a Friday morning interview on KNBR : “Just because the flow of the way the trade deadline is approaching, yes. That’s our job to do that. To talk with our counterparts around the league. We receive calls. We make calls. Just to kind of see where the market is at. I think the answer to that is yes. We’re just doing our jobs.” When asked if Lynch could tell us if he was talking to the Los Angeles Chargers about Khalil Mack, he laughed and said: “No, I can’t tell you that. I had a lot of people ask me that yesterday. We seem to be connected to everyone. I don’t know where that comes from. I had a player ask me that yesterday. It’s usually [George] Kittle. He asks about everything, which I love.” Khalil Mack is an obvious trade candidate for the 49ers. Mack said himself that San Francisco was this close to acquiring him in a trade way back in 2018 before the Chicago Bears swooped in at the last minute. Mack wouldn’t cost two first-round picks this time around. Depending on the salary retention, he could cost as low as a conditional Day 3 pick. The Chargers have little reason to hold on to the 35-year-old pending free agent at 0-5. Mack’s $10 million signing bonus has already been paid, so the 49ers would owe a little more than $6 million in 2026 salary. If you’re the 49ers, why not go younger? Mack’s teammate, Tuli Tuipulotu, is in the final year of his rookie deal. He was a second-rounder from the 2023 NFL Draft. On 10 fewer pass-rush snaps, Tuipulotu has five more pressures and a pass-rush win rate that’s five percentage points higher. He also has seven more run stops and forced two fumbles. Tuipulotu is 266 pounds, so he has no trouble holding up against the run. If the 49ers are looking at one of the Chargers’ pass rushers, the lesser-known name might be the better option.

item.title: Chelsea captain Reece James faces lengthy absence following surgery
item.description: Chelsea captain Reece James has undergone surgery -Credit:Marc Atkins, Getty Images Reece James faces a THREE-MONTH spell on the sidelines after undergoing knee surgery. James, 26, missed Chelsea's last two games either side of the international break with an injury that forced him to withdraw from the England squad last month. The Blues captain now looks unlikely to feature again before the new year. Chelsea confirmed on Friday that James has undergone a minor knee operation after sustaining the injury during a training session. A club statement read, via The Mirror : "Reece has already begun his road to recovery and will be supported by the club's medical department at Cobham during this rehabilitation phase. Everyone at Chelsea wishes Reece a speedy recovery and will support him on his road to return." Wrexham shouldn't push the panic button yet despite challenge facing Phil Parkinson Cristiano Ronaldo delivers brutal Portugal 'ultimatum' after Jorge Jesus 'broke his word' -Credit:Darren Walsh, Chelsea FC via Getty Images James previously suffered a knee injury in 2022, which saw him miss that year's FIFA World Cup. The defender's fitness improved last season, allowing him to play a prominent role for England at the 2026 edition. Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso has deployed James in midfield this season and on Friday described his absence as 'disappointing'. "It's not going to be a two or three-week thing, it's going to be longer and after that we will see," Alonso told a pre-match press conference ahead of Saturday's match away to Everton. "Before Christmas, after Christmas, time will tell. Things have to be done properly so that he feels right and is in the best possible condition. "It's a disappointment for everyone, for him, but we need to have a squad to deal with injuries. We support him, he will stay close to the team, he's a great influence even when he's not available, and we wish him the best recovery." To listen to the latest episode of 'All Out Soccer' - CLICK HERE James' injury comes at a challenging period in the schedule for the Blues. Following their clash with Everton, Chelsea welcome Tottenham Hotspur before hosting Manchester United, sandwiched around a Carabao Cup trip to Liverpool. Levi Colwill has assumed the captaincy at Chelsea since James was ruled out, and Alonso is confident he has sufficient leaders within his ranks. "We have Moi (Moises Caicedo), we have Levi, we have players who take responsibility and carry that role in a perfect way," the Spaniard stressed. "They have the support from the rest and the players respect them when they wear the armband, so it's no bother. Their own personality. Each one is different. Levi is different from Reece, Moi is different, Cole [Palmer], Hendo (Jordan Henderson). "Each one is different, Dibu (Emiliano Martínez) as well. That's why it's so important for me to have a mix of personalities, qualities and stages of their careers. I think we're in a good place in that way."

item.title: Tunji-Ojo praises Tinubu for approving lifetime pay for retired immigration chiefs
item.description: The Minister of Interior, Dr Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo has described President Bola Tinubu as a visionary leader whose policies are intended to have long term and lasting positive impact. The minister said this at the closing ceremony of the Specialised Boarder Control and Immigration Management System (BCIMS) Training at the Immigration Headquarters on Friday in Abuja. Tunji-Ojo noted that Tinubu under the renewed hope agenda, was building a system that would stand the test of time and be in full effect even after he was out of office. “President Bola Tinubu has never been about the immediate, but the future. He understands that the most prosperous nations do not boil, cook, and eat their seeds, they plant them. “What this president is doing is planting the seed so that there will be abundance for the future,” he said. The minister said that Tinubu acknowledged that he would not be in office forever, but institutions would remain forever and what mattered was what would be handed down through generations. He commended the president for putting an end to backlogs of promotions, noting that no fewer than 50,000 personnel had gained new ranks and offices in the span of three years. “It has never happened before, but Tinubu did it. He also increased the volume of recruitment, where we now have no fewer that 40,000 new recruits at once. “When it comes to salary increment, Mr President has done it. In terms of hazard allowances, peculiar allowance, he also did,” he said. Tunji-Ojo also praised Tinubu for his dedication to the welfare of both active and retired personnel, highlighting the increase in pension of retired Comptroller- Generals of Immigration. “Previously, CGs had a pension of about N130,000, it was not encouraging. But what did the president do? He signed, and approved salary for life for CGs and DCGs. “This president has cared for the services more than any president in the history of Nigeria. He has given you his all. “And all he asks from us in the service is to do our jobs well and make Nigerians happy. Everything we have asked of him, he has done. This the least we can do,” he added. The post Tunji-Ojo praises Tinubu for approving lifetime pay for retired immigration chiefs appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Police debunk report of woman cutting off husband’s manhood in Taraba
item.description: By Femi Bolaji JALINGO — The Taraba State Police Command has debunked a viral social media report alleging that a 24-year-old woman, identified as Maimuna, severed her 30-year-old husband’s manhood, leading to his death in Maigoje village, Gashaka Local Government Area of the state. The command said preliminary verification by the Divisional Police Officer (DPO) of Gashaka Division did not establish that the alleged incident occurred. In a statement issued on Friday, October 16, 2026, the Police Public Relations Officer, ASP Victor Mshelizah, on behalf of the Commissioner of Police, CP Edwin Ogbeghagha, said inquiries conducted in Maigoje village, Mai Idanu Ward and neighbouring communities found no evidence to substantiate the report. According to the police, community members and local leaders contacted during the investigation also did not confirm the allegations. The statement read, “The Taraba State Police Command has noted a publication circulating on social media alleging that a woman identified as Maimuna inflicted injuries on her husband, Haruna Ishaka, resulting in his death in Maigoje Village, Mai Idanu Ward, Gashaka LGA. “In response, the Divisional Police Officer, Gashaka Division, conducted an on-the-ground verification exercise and made inquiries within the area and surrounding communities. “The exercise did not establish the occurrence of the alleged incident, and the communities contacted did not confirm the claims. “Based on the findings, the Command has no confirmed information substantiating the report as circulated. Members of the public are therefore advised not to treat the allegations as established facts.” The Commissioner of Police urged journalists, social media influencers and members of the public to exercise restraint and verify sensitive security-related reports through official law enforcement channels before publishing or sharing them. Ogbeghagha also warned against the deliberate fabrication and dissemination of unverified information capable of causing public disquiet or damaging individuals’ reputations. He said anyone found knowingly spreading false information would face appropriate legal consequences. The command reaffirmed its commitment to protecting lives and maintaining public order in Taraba State, urging residents to report genuine security concerns to the nearest police station. The post Police debunk report of woman cutting off husband’s manhood in Taraba appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: When should fighters stop fighting?
item.description: For some, fighting is a business; make as much money from the sport as possible, and then walk away with your health intact. For others, fighting is a lifestyle; it’s a drug that you can’t just quit. There is a tendency to disregard new-age combat sports as a clown show. Whether it’s UFC fights on the White House South Lawn , former Disney kid Jake Paul becoming one of boxing’s biggest financial draws, or whatever is going on at Misfits in a given week , the bravado, theatrics and occasional buffoonery that have always accompanied the fight game have inflated to an obscene level. When the bell rings, however, the art of cracking fist, knee or shin against skull is as grisly as it’s always been. Fighters knowingly accept the risk of serious injury or death when they step into the ring. Often, those same fighters will say the feeling of vitality inside said ring is unmatched. Liverpudlian Darren Till , a former UFC star turned bare-knuckle boxer for BKFC, is in this camp. “I love violence. I love fighting. I was built for fighting,” he tells The Independent . At 33, he hasn’t even started to think about when he might give this game up. He just went the distance with a specimen many struggle to fathom is still going at such an age. Darren Till (right) beat 49-year-old Cuban boogeyman Yoel Romero (left) by decision in a blockbuster BKFC clash (BKFC) Yoel Romero is 49. An Olympic wrestling silver medallist from all the way back in 2000, Romero is most known for his truly remarkable run in the UFC, which he began aged 36 – 13 years after that triumph at the Sydney Games. Entering mixed martial arts’s premier organisation when most combatants his age begin to wind down, the Cuban boogeyman took the middleweight division by storm and went on to fight for the world title three times. With age, he has levelled up the brutality. He too now mostly fights bare-knuckle, a discipline which offers a complete lack of protection, thus facilitating some of the most sickening knockouts you’ll see. All this, while pushing half a century. And like Till, a man 16 years his junior, retirement isn’t on his mind. What’s his motivation, you might think? He doesn’t seem to have one; fighting is simply his purpose. “I don’t live a motivational life, motivation will leave you tomorrow,” Romero says through an interpreter. “It’s something that’s in my blood, it’s something that we do. I was born with the concept of: if you want to be a great athlete, you’ve got to be disciplined. You’re not an athlete if you’re not disciplined.” Even this discipline comes secondary to his faith, however. He previously said that “God will decide” when he stops fighting, though he back-tracked on that in this interview: “My faith with God is something else. It doesn’t dictate my wins or losses. It is my first battle.” Romero won’t be hanging up the gloves any time soon, it seems. He will certainly fight into his 50s, with 52 currently his touted retirement age; though this continues to be pushed

He doesn’t seem to have one; fighting is simply his purpose. “I don’t live a motivational life, motivation will leave you tomorrow,” Romero says through an interpreter. “It’s something that’s in my blood, it’s something that we do. I was born with the concept of: if you want to be a great athlete, you’ve got to be disciplined. You’re not an athlete if you’re not disciplined.” Even this discipline comes secondary to his faith, however. He previously said that “God will decide” when he stops fighting, though he back-tracked on that in this interview: “My faith with God is something else. It doesn’t dictate my wins or losses. It is my first battle.” Romero won’t be hanging up the gloves any time soon, it seems. He will certainly fight into his 50s, with 52 currently his touted retirement age; though this continues to be pushed back. He is far from the only fighter to be glued to the fight game, however. There is an obvious worry to this. Fighter health, especially in retirement, has always been one of the great concerns of combat sports. Heartbreaking stories of ex-competitors now battling CTE (chronic traumatic encephalopathy, a brain disease linked to repeated blows to the head) and pugilistic dementia are tragically common in this world. It often feels preventable; perhaps that is the greater tragedy. Romero is most known for his remarkable UFC run, which he began aged 36 (Getty Images) Nobody knows this more than Dave Harris of the Ringside Charitable Trust (RCT). Harris has spent his life in boxing, as a trainer, promoter and manager. He now works to improve the lives of ex-boxers and their families, chiefly striving to raise funds for a residential care home for retired boxers facing injury, illness and hardship. Harris is on the front line as he sees former elite athletes deteriorate physically and mentally as a result of their craft. “I've got wives sobbing down the phones because their husbands say they’re having affairs when they're not, because they’re suffering from pugilistic dementia,” he says. In a desperately sad case, Harris revealed at the time of speaking that Jimmy Revie, a former British featherweight champion, had been forced to leave his care home because of aggressive behaviour stemming from his dementia. A normal care home can’t cater to the unique needs of ex-boxers, Harris believes. “Jimmy, in a Ringside rest and care home, there will be the right people around just to calm him, talk to him, show him [his old fight] films. This home he’s in, there is nothing to keep their minds active.” Just two weeks later, Revie passed away on 13 September, aged 79. Jimmy Revie, a former British featherweight champion, died in September after a long battle with pugilistic dementia (Getty) Knowing what fighters can go through in later life, Harris cares for the wellbeing of retired boxers while also fighting for greater protection for those still active. He believes promoters and the British Boxing Board of Control ( BBBofC ) fail today’s crop. “There is an epidemic out there that nobody is acknowledging, especially the hard-nosed promoters,” he says. “The [real world] mafia kill people. Well, the boxing mafia, the ‘soft’ mafia, they don’t kill anybody. But they kill them over a long period of time because of their decisions they make. That’s an analogy that basically they let fighters go on too long. It’s my opinion that they should be doing something about it.” BBBofC general secretary Robert Smith responded to this statement by saying: “Mr Harris’ comments are extremely disappointing bearing in mind the British Boxing Board of Control’s medical standards are some of the most stringent in the world and recognised as such. Over the years the BBBofC has supported the Ringside Charitable Trust.” Harris is baffled how certain big names have been allowed to fight on. Derek Chisora is the obvious one , insisting that he will fight again in December for a world title despite his defeat to Deontay Wilder in April being billed as his 50th and final fight. But Kell Brook is another pressing case. The former IBF welterweight world champion announced in August that, at 40, he would come out of retirement for another fight, having previously admitted to mental-health struggles since calling time on his career. Kell Brook is coming out of retirement for another fight aged 40 (Action Images via Reuters) “Is that in his interest after the career he had? No. Where’s the common sense?” Harris questions. “They’ll put him in with a class act or to build somebody up – I wouldn’t be surprised if, after this September thing with Conor Benn [ his defeat to Ryan Garcia ], they put Kell Brook in with him. It’s just the way the fight game goes, but it’s wrong. The Board of Control, they want to get their act together.” He adds: “I certainly think they [the BBBofC] have a difficult job but they make it harder for themselves because they should be saying, ‘No, we will not give Kell Brook a licence.’ But money talks and that boy will fight again. I just hope he doesn’t get a brain bleed or damage later on when he’s retired.” The BBBofC confirmed that Brook has not applied for a licence at the time of writing, but “should he do so it will be considered on its own merits”. Harris highlights the difficulty for fighters to step away from the game on their own. “They’ve got nothing else to go on to,” he says, comparing the situation to soldiers leaving the military. But this makes it easy for promoters to “manipulate” boxers when they should be safeguarding them. Money will naturally be a primary reason why fighters, especially journeymen, keep going. Then for the most successful, legacy points will always be there to tick off. Mike Tyson said he took his fight with Paul in 2024, aged 58, because he’s a “glory junkie” rather t

item.title: Why Tigers are clear winners of Tarik Skubal trade with Dodgers
item.description: Why Tigers are clear winners of Tarik Skubal trade with Dodgers originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Detroit Tigers had a very disappointing 2026 MLB season. Coming into the year, the Tigers were supposed to be postseason contenders, and there was hope they'd be able to make a run in what could've been Tarik Skubal's last year with the team. However, they struggled once Skubal went down with an elbow injury and fell far enough out of the playoff race that the Tigers decided to sell, shipping Skubal out in a deal with the Los Angeles Dodgers . Trading Skubal was not a very popular decision, but now, following the Dodgers' NLCS elimination and the report from ESPN's Alden Gonzalez , the Tigers appear to be the clear winners of this Skubal trade. Tigers are winners of Tarik Skubal trade with Dodgers Gonzalez shared that, with the looming MLB lockout on December 1, "it would be really difficult for the Dodgers to justify signing Skubal to a massive deal before knowing what MLB's economic model will look like." So, with the Dodgers facing an uncertain future regarding how MLB payrolls work, the Dodgers might have to refrain from signing Skubal to a long-term deal. That means he might be leaving the Dodgers in free agency. Skubal might sign elsewhere, and a return to the Tigers could be in play. They do need starting pitching, and it would be quite the move to sign Skubal to an extension and also get the huge trade package for him at the MLB trade deadline that they got from the Dodgers. Zyhir Hope, Brady Smith, and River Ryan were the three players the Tigers got from the Dodgers in the Skubal trade. If even one of them were to turn into a quality big-leaguer, it wouldn't matter what Skubal does in free agency; it would be a win. MORE : How Mets could have advantage over Dodgers in free-agent pursuit of Tarik Skubal But, adding on the context that the Dodgers might not have the means to sign Skubal to an extension, they would've gotten just two-and-a-half months out of Skubal, failing to make the World Series, let alone winning a game in the NLCS. The Dodgers spent a fortune to acquire Skubal from the Tigers, and now he might leave the team after the Dodgers came up well short on their quest to three-peat as World Series champions. One thing should be clear following the NLCS loss for the Dodgers. Regardless of what happens with Skubal in free agency, the Tigers clearly won this trade. It might not have been a popular one for the fans at the time, but it was clearly the right decision, especially with the Dodgers failing to win the World Series in 2026. item.title: Justin Ishbia addresses Chicago railyards deal backlash, warns of cost of inaction
item.description: Justin Ishbia and Rate Field (Getty) For the first time, Justin Ishbia, the owner-in-waiting of the Chicago White Sox, spoke in a public forum about his controversial plan to place the team in his new megadevelopment at an Amtrak railyard. The White Sox currently play in Bridgeport at the publicly-owned Rate Field. In order to move the team’s home games to his new development , dubbed the Railyards, Amtrak needs a new maintenance facility and has chosen Bridgeport as its site. Needless to say, Bridgeport residents are less than thrilled about potentially losing their baseball team and in return, receiving a potentially noisy train maintenance facility just a few blocks away. While acknowledging the community pushback, Ishbia said that there’s also a cost to inaction at a Crain’s event in Fulton Market. According to the outlet, Ishbia noted that furious responses to big real estate gambles are at least partially to blame for the Bears not getting their downtown stadium in 2024 and now potentially moving across state lines to Indiana. He also encouraged residents to consider the benefits of local rail infrastructure. Ishbia’s plan for the Railyards development is contingent on Amtrak being able to move their maintenance facility to Bridgeport. Amtrak plans to use a federal exemption to be allowed to build the $900 million new facility in Bridgeport, rendering a significant chunk of the backlash a moot point. Ishbia still needs certain approvals from the City Council in order to pursue his full vision for the Railyards. Ishbia declined to fully commit to moving the White Sox, at least until he gains full control of the franchise. “I would say it’s not a foregone conclusion — the White Sox leaving. That’s a Jerry [Reinsdorf] decision. Period. End of conversation. One day I’ll have a turn, but it’s not today,” Ishbia said at the event, according to the outlet. Recently, Ishbia revealed plans for the Railyards that included renderings of a new ballpark for the White Sox. — Hunter Cooke Read more Aldermen are ratcheting up pressure on Amtrak and Ishbia’s development plan. Will it matter? Ishbia gears up for South Loop Railyards plan with $15M purchase of nearby shopping center Lawmakers interrogate Amtrak and Ishbia representatives over White Sox project This article originally appeared on The Real Deal. Click here to read the full story.

item.title: FSU vs. Miami: Score predictions, analysis from FSU Wire
item.description: The FSU Seminoles (3-3, 1-2 ACC) are back on the road, playing the Miami Hurricanes in their toughest game of the season. The Seminoles have not won a road game since 2023 and are looking to snap a two-game losing streak against the Hurricanes. While anything can happen on the football field, it will be tough for FSU to pull off the upset . Miami (5-0, 3-0), the No. 3 team in the country, is simply better at every position and has solidified itself as the top team in the ACC with a 5-0 start. They have the best offense and defense in the conference, with Heisman candidates Darian Mensah and Malachi Toney leading the offense. The defense might not have as much star power, but their defensive front is once again excellent, and they have the ability to easily pressure the quarterback, thanks to defensive ends Marquise Lightfoot and Damon Wilson II. It will be up to FSU's offensive line to have a good game to try and keep Ashton Daniels upright with room to work in the pocket. The Seminoles trail Miami 33-37 all time, and the two are tied 29-29 since they started playing every year. FSU has a winning record in Miami, going 21-20. Here are our predictions for FSU's game against Miami. Matthew Lenix Prediction: Miami 38, FSU 17 I don't see this game being particularly close. Miami has one of the best run defenses in the nation, which will likely force FSU to be one-dimensional, and their offense leads the country in scoring, which is a bad matchup for an inconsistent Seminoles' defense. Florida State will come out inspired, but Miami is just a better team. Brandon Foster Prediction: Miami 38, FSU 20 I think Florida State hangs around longer than the spread might suggest. Rivalry games tend to get weird, and FSU should come into this one with plenty of emotion after the way last week ended. Still, Miami feels like the safer pick right now. The Hurricanes are at home, they are the best team Norvell has faced this season, and Florida State has not shown enough consistency defensively for me to call the upset. Jacob Smith Prediction: Miami 67, FSU 3 Darian Mensah is playing like a Heisman-level QB, but Miami hasn't played anyone to warrant being considered No. 3. JD McCarthy Prediction: Miami 45, FSU 17 These two historic rivals are not on the same level right now, and Mario Cristobal and the Hurricanes will take the chance to hammer that home on Saturday night. The Seminoles have not won on the road since the 2023 season and are outmatched at every position on the field. Look for Malachi Toney and Darian Mensah to have another big game against a weak FSU secondary. Follow us @FSUWire on X and like our page on Facebook to follow ongoing coverage of Florida State news, notes, and opinions. This article originally appeared on FSU Wire: FSU vs. Miami: Score predictions, analysis from FSU Wire

item.title: Former Sale Sharks lock Andrews dies at team hotel in La Rochelle
item.description: Andrews joined Sale in February 2024 and made 45 appearances for the club before heading back to his native South Africa at the end of last season [Getty Images] Former Sale second row Hyron Andrews has died at his Johannesburg Lions' team hotel before their Champions Cup match at La Rochelle on Saturday. A statement from SA Rugby stated that his death had been an "accident" and that the 31-year-old had "died after a fall". "We are heartbroken by the passing of Hyron," said Lions chief executive Rudolf Straeuli. "He was not only a gifted rugby player, but also a cherished member of our Lions family having recently joined us this season. "On behalf of our chairman, Mr Altmann Allers, the board and everyone at the Lions, I extend our deepest sympathies to [Andrews' wife] Maighlin, their young sons Hendrix and Emerson and the entire Andrews family. "We stand with them in their sorrow and will remember Hyron with great affection and respect." The Lions will fulfil their fixture against La Rochelle, which kicks off at 17:30 BST, in Andrews' honour, while a moment's silence will be observed at all the opening round's fixtures. "This is terrible and distressing news; our hearts go out to Hyron's family and the whole Lions rugby community," said Mark Alexander, president of the South African Rugby Union. "There are no words to adequately convey our shock and the depth of sympathy we feel for his wife Maighlin, and for his extended family, friends, team-mates and loved ones during this time of immense sorrow. "His untimely passing is a devastating loss, and we share in the grief of all who knew and loved him." Andrews left Sale in the summer to return to his native South Africa. He made 45 appearances for the club after arriving in February 2024 from the Durban-based Sharks as injury cover for England international lock Jonny Hill. "Hyron was just a brilliant guy and a brilliant team-mate," said Sale director of rugby Alex Sanderson. "He was so skilled on the field but off it, he was always someone you would want to have a beer with. "He was funny and charismatic in his own unique, dry way and the lads, to a man, loved playing with him and being around him. "It was a big move for Hyron and his wife Maighlin to come to England, but he truly made a second home in Manchester. It was incredible to see how he and his family embraced the club and area. "Most importantly, he was a loving husband to Maighlin and a doting father to his two gorgeous boys. It was an absolute privilege to get to know him and it's just absolutely devastating for everyone." While he was yet to earn senior international honours, Andrews had represented the Junior Springboks in 2015. Andrews' death comes 10 years on from the sudden death of Munster coach Anthony Foley in Paris before a Champions Cup fixture. While he was yet to earn senior international honours, Andrews had represented the Junior Springboks in 2015. Andrews' death comes 10 years on from the sudden death of Munster coach Anthony Foley in Paris before a Champions Cup fixture. Foley, 42, died in his sleep on the eve of a match against Racing 92 after a heart condition caused fluid to build up in his lungs. Munster's present-day players will wear commemorative tops, featuring the Munster club crest and Foley's shirt number eight as part of their pre-match routine at their match against Racing on Saturday. The Lions, who play their home matches at Ellis Park, are making their first appearance in Europe's premier club competition, with South African sides introduced into the continental competition in the 2022-23 season. They have won two of their first three matches in the United Rugby Championship so far this season, including beating defending champions Leinster in their first game of their campaign. Andrews had played in all three games, making his first start for his new club in Saturday's 57-15 defeat by the Bulls. In an interview with the Mapantsula a Rugby Show, published earlier this week, Andrews talked about the various Johannesburg attractions he has visited since arriving in the city. "We work hard here, it's good to decompress, get away and spend some time with the family," he said. "When the family is happy, you are happy and it shows when you go to work." item.title: Jackson Koivun Rounds Out The Lineup For The 2026 Skins Game
item.description: PALM BEACH GARDENS, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 28: Keegan Bradley of the United States celebrates with his check after winning The Skins Game at Panther National on November 28, 2025 in Palm Beach Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Mike Ehrmann/Getty Images) Getty Images Last year saw the return of the popular golf event call the Skins Game. What used to be a staple for golf fans during the offseason stopped abruptly in 2008 returned in 2025 for Black Friday viewing. This event brings together four PGA Tour pros to compete in a friendly but high-stakes competition with a total purse of $4 million dollars. The latest iteration of the event saw the following golfers competing for big money: 2025 Skins Game Participants Keegan Bradley Xander Schauffele Shane Lowry Tommy Fleetwood For those who don’t remember how things panned out in 2025, Keegan Bradley took home the biggest chunk of the purse, winning 11 skins for a total prize of $2.1 million, while Tommy Fleetwood earned $1.7 million, and Shane Lowry managed to win one skin for $200,000. If you do your math, you would realize the purse money was exhausted with the above golfers, which meant Xander Schauffele was left with a big fat $0 at the end of the event. The event’s rebirth was deemed a success, and the 2026 field has been finalized with the event just over a month away. 2026 Skins Game Details Date: Nov. 27, 2026 Where: The Atlantic Fields Club Location: Hobe Sound, Florida Participants: Justin Thomas Wyndham Clark Brooks Koepka Jackson Koivun How to watch: Amazon Prime Video Time: 9:00am EST Purse: $4 million dollars As for the format of the event, the Skins Game is going back to its roots. The competition itself will return to the original format, which started back in 1983. Last year they tried the “reverse purse” twist, in which each player started with $1 million and the amount went up or down based on whether a player won or lost a hole. For many viewers and spectators, it didn’t resound as much as the older format. The old format, for those who don’t remember, has each player starting at $0, making every hole’s value clearer and more obvious. Each hole carries a dollar value and tied holes will roll over, which can raise the stakes rather quickly. All golfers involved in this year’s event are first-time players in the Skins Game, but it was Justin Thomas who was slated to be in last year’s event before undergoing offseason back surgery and having to remove himself from the field. Outside of Koivun , the participants in the Skins Game in 2026 are all multi-major champions on the PGA Tour. Wyndham Clark is a two-time U.S. Open champion, Justin Thomas is a two-time PGA Championship winner, and Brooke Koepka brings a resume with two U.S. Open titles and three PGA Championship crowns. For golf fans who both love the history of the Skins Game, and who are starved for the game during the offseason months, the Skins Game is a great event to quench that proverbial thirst on a day which will showcase plenty

If you do your math, you would realize the purse money was exhausted with the above golfers, which meant Xander Schauffele was left with a big fat $0 at the end of the event. The event’s rebirth was deemed a success, and the 2026 field has been finalized with the event just over a month away. 2026 Skins Game Details Date: Nov. 27, 2026 Where: The Atlantic Fields Club Location: Hobe Sound, Florida Participants: Justin Thomas Wyndham Clark Brooks Koepka Jackson Koivun How to watch: Amazon Prime Video Time: 9:00am EST Purse: $4 million dollars As for the format of the event, the Skins Game is going back to its roots. The competition itself will return to the original format, which started back in 1983. Last year they tried the “reverse purse” twist, in which each player started with $1 million and the amount went up or down based on whether a player won or lost a hole. For many viewers and spectators, it didn’t resound as much as the older format. The old format, for those who don’t remember, has each player starting at $0, making every hole’s value clearer and more obvious. Each hole carries a dollar value and tied holes will roll over, which can raise the stakes rather quickly. All golfers involved in this year’s event are first-time players in the Skins Game, but it was Justin Thomas who was slated to be in last year’s event before undergoing offseason back surgery and having to remove himself from the field. Outside of Koivun , the participants in the Skins Game in 2026 are all multi-major champions on the PGA Tour. Wyndham Clark is a two-time U.S. Open champion, Justin Thomas is a two-time PGA Championship winner, and Brooke Koepka brings a resume with two U.S. Open titles and three PGA Championship crowns. For golf fans who both love the history of the Skins Game, and who are starved for the game during the offseason months, the Skins Game is a great event to quench that proverbial thirst on a day which will showcase plenty of sports action. So, before Black Friday shopping, NBA basketball, and NFL football, what better way to kick off your Black Friday than with the 2026 Skins Game? This article was originally published on Forbes.com

item.title: Doug Gottlieb hangs up on Rob Parker after demanding apology
item.description: Credit: Green Bay Phoenix, Fox Sports Radio Doug Gottlieb and Rob Parker used to be Fox Sports Radio colleagues, but now they can’t get through a two-minute phone call. In his third season as head men’s basketball coach at the University of Wisconsin-Green Bay, Gottlieb has supported the proposed Protect College Sports Act, and three weeks ago, while speaking to reporters , he addressed the state of college athletics by arguing coaches are more important than players. @GottliebShow joins @OddCoupleFSR to discuss his take that coaches are more important than players in the NIL era and it got HEATED between Doug and @robparkerMLBbro https://t.co/ecHILbKBCC — FOX Sports Radio (@FoxSportsRadio) October 15, 2026 “Coaches are way more important than players,” Gottlieb said. “Because they just do more. Coaches don’t leave every year the way that players leave every year.” Gottlieb joined Fox Sports Radio’s The Odd Couple, hosted by Rob Parker and Kelvin Washington, to defend his take. But the conversation immediately turned contentious when Gottlieb demanded an apology and accused Parker of misrepresenting his quote about coaches being more important than players. After playing the full quote, Parker asked, “You stand by that players don’t matter? Coaches are more important than players…” Gottlieb quickly interjected, saying what Parker just said was “bullcrap,” noting he never said, “players don’t matter.” “You said I said players don’t matter,” Gottlieb fired back. “Not only is it unfair, it’s not true and it’s the problem with media. This is not an all-or-nothing proposal. In no world is it all or nothing. Zero.” Before continuing the interview, Gottlieb demanded an apology from Parker for misquoting him, which he did not receive. Instead of apologizing, Parker threatened to hang up on Gottlieb. “I’m not doing that,” Parker said of the apology. “Doug, if you came here for an apology party, I’ll hang up on you right now. I’m not doing that… I’m not apologizing two minutes in.” But before Parker could hang up, Gottlieb hung up on Parker, abruptly ending the interview after just two minutes. Parker told Gottlieb not to call back, not that it anyone really expected the college basketball coach to pick up the phone again after already hanging up. “That’s why you don’t have a show,” Parker ranted. “I’m glad you hung up. Don’t call back here. In fact, turn to ESPN. Go listen to Jim Rome. You better not be listening to this show… Doug is ridiculous. What kind of system doesn’t allow the players to be involved in the bargaining of this?” That’s a fair question. And maybe he could have pressed Gottlieb on it if he hadn’t started the interview by misquoting him. Gottlieb later called Parker’s comment “ embarrassing ,” noting he used to consider his former Fox Sports Radio colleague a friend. item.title: Real Madrid’s Vinícius Jr. appeal rejected
item.description: Real Madrid’s Vinícius Jr. appeal rejected La Liga giants Real Madrid have on Friday been dealt a blow on the personnel front. This comes amid confirmation that the club’s appeal to have Vinícius Jr’s suspension overturned has been rejected. Wide-man Vinícius was of course hit with a heavy sanction on the part of the Spanish football authorities earlier this week. After being shown a straight red card for pulling the hair of Villarreal’s Nathan Saliba during a La Liga clash last weekend, the 26-year-old was banned for four domestic fixtures. Of the collective opinion that this was too severe, the Real Madrid board, in turn, launched an appeal to have the number of games reduced. As alluded to above, however, on Friday, Los Blancos have officially seen their plea rejected. As per a report from journalist Fabrizio Romano: ‘Real Madrid appeal for Vini Jr’s 4-games ban in La Liga has been rejected.’ The Brazilian is therefore primed to sit out all of his side’s upcoming fixtures against Sevilla, Barcelona, Racing Santander and Valencia. Conor Laird – GSFN

item.title: Arsenal to retake team photo with Saliba after defender’s omission — Arteta
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta has confirmed that the club will take a new team photograph featuring William Saliba after the defender was surprisingly left out of the official 2026/27 picture published this week. According to Sky Sports, Arteta said the original photo was arranged to meet commercial commitments after earlier attempts had been cancelled, and confirmed Saliba was “completely fine” about missing it, after being unavailable to attend due to a medical appointment. The omission surprised supporters, particularly because Saliba remains a key member of the squad. The 25-year-old has yet to play this season because of a back injury, but has made 184 appearances for Arsenal. “We will have another picture with the whole family,” Arteta said ahead of Arsenal’s trip to Nottingham Forest. “Hopefully we can get them all together at some point one day, and we’ll announce that as well.” The Arsenal boss said Saliba had been unable to attend and had taken the situation in good humour, despite some banter from teammates. The club plans to arrange a new photograph with the full squad. Saliba has resumed training on the grass as he continues his recovery. Arteta said the defender is progressing well and is due to have another MRI scan next week to assess the healing process. “Every sign so far has been very, very positive,” Arteta said. “It will be good to have him.” Arteta also said Martin Zubimendi could return against Forest after picking up an injury during the warm-down following the Leeds match. Piero Hincapie is expected to be out for another one or two weeks, while Christos Tzolis is making good progress from a hamstring injury sustained on international duty with Greece. The post Arsenal to retake team photo with Saliba after defender’s omission — Arteta appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Artemis II Heat Shield After Splashdown
item.description: US Navy Shortly after NASA’s Artemis II mission splashed down on April 10, 2026, U.S. Navy divers captured underwater imagery of the Orion spacecraft’s heat shield. In the months after, the agency measured whether the thermal protection system effectively safeguarded the crew and Orion systems as the spacecraft reentered Earth’s atmosphere. This rigorous analysis confirmed that the heat shield performed as expected. Learn how Orion’s heat shield was examined. Image credit: US Navy

item.title: Sally Rooney's books no longer sold in UK over support for banned pro-Palestinian group
item.description: Irish novelist Sally ⁠Rooney's books will ​no longer be sold in Britain over her plans to use her royalties ​to support Palestine Action, a pro-Palestinian group banned as a terrorist organisation, Rooney and her publisher said on Wednesday. The bestselling author, known for novels including "Normal People" and "Conversations with ​Friends", has ‌been a vocal supporter of Palestine Action, including after ⁠it was proscribed by the British government under terrorism laws last year.

item.title: Argentine demonstration over education cuts ends in clashes
item.description: Argentine demonstrators clashed with police on Thursday at a major protest in Buenos Aires over budget-slashing President Javier Milei's higher education spending. The main demonstration outside parliament by thousands of university students and staff, trade unionists and opposition activists remained peaceful. But dozens of mostly hooded demonstrators who broke away from the crowd lobbed stones and other projectiles at the police, who responded with tear gas and water cannons.
