item.title: Police debunk viral report of woman severing husband’s manhood in Taraba
item.description: By Femi Bolaji Taraba State Police Command has officially debunked a widely circulated news report alleging that a 24-year-old woman, Maimuna, cut off her 30-year-old husband’s manhood, leading to his death in Maigoje village, Gashaka Local Government Area. In a press statement issued on Friday, October 16, 2026, by the Police Public Relations Officer, ASP Victor Mshelizah, on behalf of the State Commissioner of Police, CP Edwin Ogbeghagha, the command stated that an on-the-ground investigation conducted by the Divisional Police Officer (DPO), Gashaka Division, found no evidence supporting the claim. According to the command, fact-finding missions across Maigoje village, Mai Idanu Ward, and neighbouring settlements revealed that no such incident occurred, adding that community members and local leaders refuted the allegations contained in the viral publication. The statement read: “The Taraba State Police Command has noted a publication circulating on social media alleging that a woman identified as Maimuna inflicted injuries on her husband, Haruna Ishaka, resulting in his death in Maigoje Village, Mai Idanu Ward, Gashaka LGA. “In response, the Divisional Police Officer, Gashaka Division, conducted an on-the-ground verification exercise and made inquiries within the area and surrounding communities. “The exercise did not establish the occurrence of the alleged incident, and the communities contacted did not confirm the claims. “Based on the findings, the Command has no confirmed information substantiating the report as circulated. Members of the public are therefore advised not to treat the allegations as established facts.” The Commissioner of Police, CP Edwin Ogbeghagha, urged journalists, social media influencers, and the general public to exercise restraint and rigorously verify sensitive security stories with official law enforcement channels before going to press. Ogbeghagha warned against the deliberate fabrication or dissemination of unverified reports capable of causing public disquiet or damaging individual reputations, adding that anyone found knowingly spreading false information would face appropriate legal consequences. The command reassured residents of Taraba State of its continued dedication to safeguarding lives and maintaining public order, encouraging citizens to report genuine security issues directly to the nearest police station. The post Police debunk viral report of woman severing husband’s manhood in Taraba appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Gov Fubara Rewards Real Madrid Academy Players, Officials With ₦50 Million After UK Tour
item.description: Rivers State Governor, Siminalayi Fubara, has awarded ₦50 million to players and coaches of the state-sponsored Real Madrid Academy following their participation in an international football tour of Southampton, United Kingdom. Governor Fubara announced the reward when the academy’s management, officials and players visited him at Government House in Port Harcourt to present a trophy they won during the tour. The delegation comprised 60 students and 12 staff members who participated in the international football engagement, providing the young players with an opportunity to develop their skills, gain international exposure and experience football beyond their immediate environment. The governor commended the academy’s management and officials for their commitment to nurturing young talents, while particularly applauding the students for their discipline and good conduct throughout the trip. The governor commended the academy’s management and officials for their commitment to nurturing young talents. Fubara acknowledged that the academy, which combines academic education with structured football training, was established by his predecessor. He, however, stressed that his administration would sustain the initiative, explaining that the continuity of beneficial programmes should not be determined by who initiated them. He said his commitment was to policies and projects capable of improving the socio-economic well-being of the people, irrespective of the administration under which they began. The governor also pledged to immediately commence efforts to address the academy’s infrastructure and funding challenges, assuring the management that the government would work towards creating a more conducive environment for the students to pursue their academic and sporting ambitions. Governor Fubara urged the young players to take both their education and football training seriously, noting that while professional football offers significant financial opportunities, academic qualifications remain important for their future. He highlighted the enormous economic potential of the global football industry, encouraging the students to recognise the opportunities available to talented players who combine discipline, hard work and determination. The governor explained that the essence of the international tour was to expose the students to the realities of football on the global stage, broaden their outlook and build their confidence to compete beyond their local environment. He expressed satisfaction with reports that some of the academy’s players had attracted interest from international football teams seeking to recruit them. He described such developments as encouraging signs of the opportunities that international exposure could create for the young talents. In their separate remarks, Secretary to the State Government, Dagogo Wokoma; the academy’s principal, Prudence Isaac-Harry; the tour facilitator, and former Super Eagles player Ida Peterson, commended Gov
item.dc:creator: Alexander Okere

In their separate remarks, Secretary to the State Government, Dagogo Wokoma; the academy’s principal, Prudence Isaac-Harry; the tour facilitator, and former Super Eagles player Ida Peterson, commended Governor Fubara for sustaining government sponsorship of the academy and supporting the students’ participation in the international football programme. item.title: The new Apple TV 4K just got its first (very small) discount
item.description: The new Apple TV 4K will be available in November. | Image: The Verge Earlier this week, Apple announced its new Apple TV 4K , which costs nearly twice as much as the 2022 model did at launch. Amazon is now offering the first discount on the forthcoming streaming box (coming out on November 13th), just days after discounting Apple’s new smart display for the first time. Right now, you can preorder the latest Apple TV 4K ahead of its November 13th release date for $289.99 ($9 off) at Amazon . Yes, it’s a tiny discount, but every little bit helps given the higher price tag. Apple TV 4K (2026) Where to Buy: $299 $289.99 at Amazon Powered by the new A19 chip, Apple’s latest streaming device now features support for Siri AI out of the box, which is coming to older Apple TV 4K models via a software update. Unlike its predecessors, though, the new model features far-field microphones so you can quickly make hands-free requests. You can, for example, ask for recommendations, like nature documentaries available on Apple TV, or ask questions about what you’re watching. Siri AI can also understand personal context, too, so long as you have an iPhone or iPad connected to your account that supports Apple Intelligence. Apple has made a few other welcome upgrades, though — as my colleague John Higgins points out — not as many as some may have expected. While Apple skipped features we’d hope to see on a $300 streamer, like audio passthrough and support for 120fps output, it’s nice that the Siri Remote now supports Find My precision tracking, so you can make it ring when it goes missing or use the Find My app on your iPhone to pinpoint its location. The new Apple TV 4K also supports a more expansive surround-sound setup, allowing you to pair up to four compatible HomePod speakers instead of just two. Read our hands-on impressions of the fourth-generation Apple TV 4K. Three more Verge-approved deals: If you’ve been meaning to pick up Pikmin 4 , Walmart is selling a digital copy for $39.88 ($20 off), which is a great price considering most other retailers are still charging the full $59.99. It’s the original Switch version, but you can upgrade to the forthcoming Nintendo Switch 2 Edition when it arrives on November 12th by purchasing a separate $9.99 upgrade pack, which adds improved graphics and a new Dandori Academy mode. That brings your total to just $49.87, saving you about $20 compared to buying the $69.99 Switch 2 Edition outright. Read our review. All eyes might be on the iPhone Duo — which is now available to preorder , despite shipments being delayed into 2027 — but if you have a non-foldable iPhone, Woot is currently discounting a wide range of Otterbox cases through October 31st. I’ve owned several of the brand’s cases for both my smartphones and tablets over the years, and I’ve been impressed by their durability. I currently use the OtterBox Symmetry Series Clear Case for my iPhone 16, which normally costs $49.99 but is now available in various colors

item.title: 7 Years Later, Apple’s Gaming Push Has Proven Surprisingly Resilient
item.description: The latest example of that came this week as Apple launched an App Store event dubbed Indie Games Week. The week-long initiative saw Apple welcoming games like Vampire Crawlers to iOS and announcing an ambitious mobile version of No Man’s Sky . At the center of that push was Carson Oliver, the new head of App Store Worldwide following Phil Schiller’s sudden departure from the role this past August. The fact that one of his first acts in the role was spearheading an indie gaming showcase hints at where Oliver’s priorities might lie.

item.title: 'Mission: 60s' event promises passport back to the Space Age
item.description: null Your invitation to revisit the Space Age has arrived. Whether you miss the days when people got dressed up to fly or you wish your "other" ride was a rocket , Mission: 60s has a *space* reserved for you. "This is a three-day celebration of Apollo , aviation, space exploration and 1960s culture," reads a promo for the Oct. 23 to 25 event in New York. "You will be fully immersed in the sights, sounds and spirit of the 1960s Space Age." "The weekend features astronauts, Apollo flight directors, Mission Control engineers, Star Trek legends, space artists, a Saturday Spacefarer Soiree with live music (1960s attire encouraged!), and a Sunday NASA Artemis keynote." Organized by Luna Replicas, a company specializing in vintage space gear, and Space for Humanity, a nonprofit that underwrites spaceflight experiences, Mission: 60s is aimed at being the bridge between the last time humanity reached for the moon and today's " second space race " to do it again — this time to stay. Mission: 60s at the TWA Hotel, Oct. 23-25, 2026, includes a tour of the 1964 World's Fair site and its NASA Apollo-era rocket displays. (Image credit: Mission 60s) Launch pad Your journey back to the 60s begins when you check into the TWA Hotel at the John F. Kennedy International Airport (JFK) in New York. Once a functioning terminal for Trans World Airlines (as featured in the 2002 movie "Catch Me If You Can"), the TWA Flight Center has been reimagined as a hotel like no other. "At the center of the hotel is Eero Saarinen's iconic TWA Flight Center, where restaurants, bars and retail outlets have taken flight. Two hotel wings, designed to reflect and defer to the landmark TWA Flight Center, sit behind the historic building and contain 512 guest rooms with views of JFK's runways and the TWA Flight Center," reads the hotel's website . The TWA Hotel is only the first sight straight out of the past that guests will encounter. On Friday (Oct. 23), Mission: 60s begins with a guided tour of the 1964 World's Fair site in Flushing Meadows. Today the home to the New York Hall of Science, the outdoor exhibits includes the Rocket Park, where Gemini-Titan II and Mercury-Atlas D rockets and a Saturn V F-1 engine still stand. "The space age was less than 10 years old when rockets like these powered incredible missions to outer space," reads the description on the museum's website. "Visitors will learn about the history of these vehicles as well as the United States' mission to reach the moon." Also on view at the World's Fair site is the Unisphere, a spherical stainless steel representation of Earth , and the Astro-View Observation Towers (later reimagined as actual flying saucers in the 1997 movie "Men in Black"). The first day concludes with Space For Humanity's (separately-ticketed) " Celestial Soiree " and a Mission: 60's pool party on the hotel's rooftop. item.dc:creator: Robert Z. Pearlman

"This is a three-day celebration of Apollo , aviation, space exploration and 1960s culture," reads a promo for the Oct. 23 to 25 event in New York. "You will be fully immersed in the sights, sounds and spirit of the 1960s Space Age." "The weekend features astronauts, Apollo flight directors, Mission Control engineers, Star Trek legends, space artists, a Saturday Spacefarer Soiree with live music (1960s attire encouraged!), and a Sunday NASA Artemis keynote." Organized by Luna Replicas, a company specializing in vintage space gear, and Space for Humanity, a nonprofit that underwrites spaceflight experiences, Mission: 60s is aimed at being the bridge between the last time humanity reached for the moon and today's " second space race " to do it again — this time to stay. Mission: 60s at the TWA Hotel, Oct. 23-25, 2026, includes a tour of the 1964 World's Fair site and its NASA Apollo-era rocket displays. (Image credit: Mission 60s) Launch pad Your journey back to the 60s begins when you check into the TWA Hotel at the John F. Kennedy International Airport (JFK) in New York. Once a functioning terminal for Trans World Airlines (as featured in the 2002 movie "Catch Me If You Can"), the TWA Flight Center has been reimagined as a hotel like no other. "At the center of the hotel is Eero Saarinen's iconic TWA Flight Center, where restaurants, bars and retail outlets have taken flight. Two hotel wings, designed to reflect and defer to the landmark TWA Flight Center, sit behind the historic building and contain 512 guest rooms with views of JFK's runways and the TWA Flight Center," reads the hotel's website . The TWA Hotel is only the first sight straight out of the past that guests will encounter. On Friday (Oct. 23), Mission: 60s begins with a guided tour of the 1964 World's Fair site in Flushing Meadows. Today the home to the New York Hall of Science, the outdoor exhibits includes the Rocket Park, where Gemini-Titan II and Mercury-Atlas D rockets and a Saturn V F-1 engine still stand. "The space age was less than 10 years old when rockets like these powered incredible missions to outer space," reads the description on the museum's website. "Visitors will learn about the history of these vehicles as well as the United States' mission to reach the moon." Also on view at the World's Fair site is the Unisphere, a spherical stainless steel representation of Earth , and the Astro-View Observation Towers (later reimagined as actual flying saucers in the 1997 movie "Men in Black"). The first day concludes with Space For Humanity's (separately-ticketed) " Celestial Soiree " and a Mission: 60's pool party on the hotel's rooftop. MCC, ILC and ILM Saturday and Sunday at Mission: 60s will bring together members of Mission Control (MCC), spaceflight experts (including ILC Dover, makers of the Apollo spacesuit ) and representatives from the Hollywood community who brought about the 60s-era visions of space exploration (including Industrial Light & Magic [ILM]) for a series of engaging panel discussions. Among the various topics scheduled for the two days of talks are: Apollo Mission Control & Flight Operations Apollo to Artemis & Beyond Women in Aerospace Apollo Communications: The Sights & Sounds From the Moon SciFi Inspires The Overview Effect Making Space Real: Art & Visual Effects That Sold Humanity on Space Space Advocacy Mission: 60s includes two full days of discussion panels spanning topics such as the Apollo spacesuit to the role of sci-fi in inspiring space exploration. (Image credit: Mission 60s) Featured speakers and moderators include Apollo flight director Gerry Griffin, TIME Magazine science editor Jeffrey Kluger, former NASA astronauts Nicole Stott and Ron Garan, "Star Trek" actor Bob Picardo and researcher Frank White. On Saturday evening, there will be a second gala, "The Spacefarer Soiree," featuring a limited meet and greet aboard a Lockheed Constellation airliner and music by Bonnie Gordon. Set in 1969, attendees are encouraged to come wearing their finest period clothing. Then, on Sunday afternoon, Uplift Aerospace will host a shared "Overview" VR experience for up to 50 people participating together. Both days will include a vendor and artists' hall, with guests signing autographs and their books, as well as companies such as NASA's official patch provider A-B Emblem, selling Apollo-themed souvenirs and memorabilia. A weekend pass is $150 per person, with add-ons for VIP access, the galas and Friday's World Fair excursion. Single-day admission is $85.

item.title: Why can you see the moon during the day? This week is the perfect time to find out
item.description: null I know perfectly well that the moon comes out during the day. I have known this for decades. Yet whenever I spot it in a blue afternoon sky, some primitive part of my brain still thinks it has turned up early. I'm certainly not the only one. Many people don't understand how it could be visible in daylight. In their eyes, the moon is a nighttime object. Why? Because that's when they notice it — it appears brighter. We tend to think of the sun as belonging to the day and the moon to the night because that's how they're usually presented to us as children. Astronomically, it makes little sense. The moon spends plenty of time above our horizon while the sun is also up — it spends half its time in the daytime sky, in fact. If the moon, pale but unmistakable, looks slightly out of place against a blue sky , it's not — you are. This week is a great time to get used to seeing it there. Just past first quarter, the moon will spend each afternoon hanging in the daytime sky, becoming easier to spot as the sun sinks towards the horizon. What's happening and when to look The moon reached first quarter on Sunday, Oct. 18, and is now waxing toward full moon, which occurs early on Monday, Oct. 26 (Oct. 25 in some time zones). That puts it in the right part of its orbit to be conspicuous during the late afternoon this weekend. Here's the useful bit to remember. Around first quarter, the moon rises roughly around midday. As it waxes towards full, it rises progressively later in the afternoon. By full moon, it rises around sunset. The moon reached first quarter on Oct. 18. (Image credit: Taro Hama @ e-kamakura via Getty Images) That makes the days immediately after first quarter an excellent time to get into the habit of finding the moon before sunset. On Monday, Oct. 19, look southeast in the afternoon for a moon just over half-lit. Each afternoon this week, it will become a little more illuminated, move farther east against the background stars, and appear progressively later in the day. You don't need to wait until dusk. In fact, that's the point. Start looking during the afternoon, when the sun is still well above the horizon. Once you find the moon, it can be surprisingly conspicuous against the blue sky. How and when I'm watching it The moon is now waxing towards being full, so it's already in the sky by dusk. (Image credit: 5c5q2cnvmg / 500px via Getty Images) I'll start looking in the mid-to-late afternoon this week, when the waxing moon should already be high enough to find easily. You can check the exact moonrise time where you are , but there's no need to catch it as it rises. Look towards the east or southeast and scan the blue sky. Once you've found the moon in daylight, keep checking on it as sunset approaches. The moon doesn't suddenly become brighter, of course. item.dc:creator: Jamie Carter
item.content:encoded: null I know perfectly well that the moon comes out during the day. I have known this for decades. Yet whenever I spot it in a blue afternoon sky, some primitive part of my brain still thinks it has turned up early. I'm certainly not the only one. Many people don't understand how it could be visible in daylight. In their eyes, the moon is a nighttime object. Why? Because that's when they notice it — it appears brighter. We tend to think of the sun as belonging to the day and the moon to the night because that's how they're usually presented to us as children. Astronomically, it makes little sense. The moon spends plenty of time above our horizon while the sun is also up — it spends half its time in the daytime sky, in fact. If the moon, pale but unmistakable, looks slightly out of place against a blue sky , it's not — you are. This week is a great time to get used to seeing it there. Just past first quarter, the moon will spend each afternoon hanging in the daytime sky, becoming easier to spot as the sun sinks towards the horizon. What's happening and when to look The moon reached first quarter on Sunday, Oct. 18, and is now waxing toward full moon, which occurs early on Monday, Oct. 26 (Oct. 25 in some time zones). That puts it in the right part of its orbit to be conspicuous during the late afternoon this weekend. Here's the useful bit to remember. Around first quarter, the moon rises roughly around midday. As it waxes towards full, it rises progressively later in the afternoon. By full moon, it rises around sunset. The moon reached first quarter on Oct. 18. (Image credit: Taro Hama @ e-kamakura via Getty Images) That makes the days immediately after first quarter an excellent time to get into the habit of finding the moon before sunset. On Monday, Oct. 19, look southeast in the afternoon for a moon just over half-lit. Each afternoon this week, it will become a little more illuminated, move farther east against the background stars, and appear progressively later in the day. You don't need to wait until dusk. In fact, that's the point. Start looking during the afternoon, when the sun is still well above the horizon. Once you find the moon, it can be surprisingly conspicuous against the blue sky. How and when I'm watching it The moon is now waxing towards being full, so it's already in the sky by dusk. (Image credit: 5c5q2cnvmg / 500px via Getty Images) I'll start looking in the mid-to-late afternoon this week, when the waxing moon should already be high enough to find easily. You can check the exact moonrise time where you are , but there's no need to catch it as it rises. Look towards the east or southeast and scan the blue sky. Once you've found the moon in daylight, keep checking on it as sunset approaches. The moon doesn't suddenly become brighter, of course. Instead, the surrounding sky darkens, increasing the contrast until the pale daytime moon seems to switch on at dusk and grow increasingly brilliant. Binoculars will give you a superb view at dusk, particularly along the terminator — the boundary between lunar day and night. That's where low-angle sunlight throws mountains and crater rims into sharp relief. As the moon waxes this week, the terminator will move steadily across its surface, revealing a different landscape each afternoon. That's another reason not to wait for the full moon. The full moon gets most of the attention, but the week beforehand is arguably a much better time to get to know our nearest celestial neighbor — and you don't even have to wait until dark. Stargazer's corner: October 23-29, 2026 The full moon arrives on Monday, Oct. 26. (Image credit: Westend61 via Getty Images) This is a bright-moon week. Full moon arrives early on Monday, Oct. 26, so moonlight will wash out faint stars and make galaxies and nebulas much harder to see. So go for Saturn instead. It reached opposition earlier this month and remains very well placed in the evening sky. Better still, the nearly full moon passes near Saturn around Oct. 23-24, giving beginners a convenient landmark for locating the planet. The moon's glare will hide faint nearby stars, but Saturn itself is easily bright enough to cope. A good example will be Oct. 27, when the Pleiades is passed closely by a bright moon. The Seven Sisters therefore won't be at their best, so you'll need to use binoculars — if you do, you'll see them easily enough. Constellation of the week: Auriga Auriga is one of the easiest constellations to find in the Northern Hemisphere's winter night sky. (Image credit: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani) Auriga, "the Charioteer," is climbing in the northeastern and eastern sky during late October evenings. It's easiest to find if you start at Capella, one of the brightest stars in the entire night sky. It's just 43 light-years from the sun. From there, I look for the other stars that form Auriga's rough pentagon, including Menkalinan, Mahasim and Almaaz. The fifth corner is Elnath, although it officially belongs to neighboring Taurus . Auriga gets even better with binoculars. The Milky Way runs straight through it, bringing with it three bright open star clusters — M36, M37 and M38. All three show up in binoculars under a reasonably dark sky, while a small telescope starts to resolve them into individual stars. There's always another layer to find in the night sky. My latest stargazing obsession There's something special about stargazing during the blue hour — that brief transition when daylight drains from the sky and night's window begins to open. It's particularly beautiful a few days before full moon, when the near-full orb is already rising in the east as the sun sets in the west. Look below it, and you may also see the Belt of Venus, a pinkish band above the eastern horizon caused by reddened sunlight shining through Earth's atmosphere , with our planet's dark blue-gray shadow beneath. As the sky fades through ever-deeper shades of blue, the moon brightens, and the first stars emerge around it.

item.title: Hardship: Ulasi says opposition failing to win voters’ support
item.description: *Predicts Obi could defeat Tinubu in Lagos By Juliet Umeh A chieftain of the Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, Dan Ulasi, has said opposition parties are failing to turn Nigerians’ concerns over the rising cost of living into political support, despite public frustration over food prices and the cost of petrol. Ulasi also predicted that National Democratic Party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, could defeat President Bola Tinubu in Lagos in the 2027 general election. Speaking on Arise Television’s Morning Show, Ulasi said the opposition had not effectively made its case to Nigerians or presented clear alternatives to the policies of the All Progressives Congress, APC-led government. “There are a lot of things to exploit, but whether they’re effectively doing it is another question,” he said. Asked whether opposition parties were making the most of public dissatisfaction, Ulasi replied: “I don’t think they’re effectively doing it. I’m going to be honest to myself.” He said opposition candidates and party leaders should be holding town hall meetings across the country to explain their plans and engage voters. “You would at this point be seeing town hall meetings from zone to zone. I don’t see it happening. Nigerians are waiting for such information to feed us, and they’re not doing it.” Ulasi said the opposition was more divided than it had been ahead of the 2023 election, making it harder to challenge an incumbent president with access to state resources. “As things are on the ground, it will take some magic for anybody to stop Tinubu. The opposition is still fragmented now, worse than it was in 2023.” The PDP chieftain, who said he supports Obi, argued that the former Anambra State governor could make strong gains in several parts of the country, including Lagos, where Tinubu served as governor before becoming president. “This time around, he will beat Tinubu in Lagos State,” Ulasi said. He argued that voters in the state were questioning what they had gained from having a former Lagos governor as president. “The Lagos people, whether Yoruba or not, cannot tell you exactly that this is our son who has been president and what they have profited from it,” he said. Ulasi challenged Tinubu to hold town hall meetings across the country and explain his administration’s record to voters. “I want him to have a town hall meeting, zone to zone, telling every zone in this country what his government has done,” he said. He said Nigerians would have to protect their votes, while stressing that a fair election would be necessary for voters’ preferences to determine the outcome. “If there is a free and fair vote in this country, Peter Obi will make less than 50 per cent of votes in most states in the North,” he said. item.content:encoded: *Predicts Obi could defeat Tinubu in Lagos By Juliet Umeh A chieftain of the Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, Dan Ulasi, has said opposition parties are failing to turn Nigerians’ concerns over the rising cost of living into political support, despite public frustration over food prices and the cost of petrol. Ulasi also predicted that National Democratic Party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, could defeat President Bola Tinubu in Lagos in the 2027 general election. Speaking on Arise Television’s Morning Show, Ulasi said the opposition had not effectively made its case to Nigerians or presented clear alternatives to the policies of the All Progressives Congress, APC-led government. “There are a lot of things to exploit, but whether they’re effectively doing it is another question,” he said. Asked whether opposition parties were making the most of public dissatisfaction, Ulasi replied: “I don’t think they’re effectively doing it. I’m going to be honest to myself.” He said opposition candidates and party leaders should be holding town hall meetings across the country to explain their plans and engage voters. “You would at this point be seeing town hall meetings from zone to zone. I don’t see it happening. Nigerians are waiting for such information to feed us, and they’re not doing it.” Ulasi said the opposition was more divided than it had been ahead of the 2023 election, making it harder to challenge an incumbent president with access to state resources. “As things are on the ground, it will take some magic for anybody to stop Tinubu. The opposition is still fragmented now, worse than it was in 2023.” The PDP chieftain, who said he supports Obi, argued that the former Anambra State governor could make strong gains in several parts of the country, including Lagos, where Tinubu served as governor before becoming president. “This time around, he will beat Tinubu in Lagos State,” Ulasi said. He argued that voters in the state were questioning what they had gained from having a former Lagos governor as president. “The Lagos people, whether Yoruba or not, cannot tell you exactly that this is our son who has been president and what they have profited from it,” he said. Ulasi challenged Tinubu to hold town hall meetings across the country and explain his administration’s record to voters. “I want him to have a town hall meeting, zone to zone, telling every zone in this country what his government has done,” he said. He said Nigerians would have to protect their votes, while stressing that a fair election would be necessary for voters’ preferences to determine the outcome. “If there is a free and fair vote in this country, Peter Obi will make less than 50 per cent of votes in most states in the North,” he said. Ulasi added that the opposition’s prospects would depend not only on public dissatisfaction with the government, but also on whether its parties could organise effectively and offer voters a credible alternative. item.title: Real Madrid demand La Liga president resign over Goebbels comparison
item.description: Javier Tebas accuses Madrid of ‘propaganda techniques’ Club want ‘immediate resignation’ for ‘constant attacks’ Real Madrid have again demanded the resignation of the president of La Liga after he compared the club’s efforts to discredit referees with the propaganda techniques of the Nazi Germany. Javier Tebas lashed out at Madrid on Friday on social media with a long post that criticised how its club television channel says referees hurt its chances of winning. The channel regularly runs reels of what it considers gross errors by match officials who are set to work upcoming games for the 15-time European champions. Continue reading...

item.title: Cost-of-living demonstrations to grip pre-election France
item.description: After weeks of student protests, France is set to be swept by broader, nationwide demonstrations Saturday over the cost of living, setting up a potentially fraught period ahead of presidential elections next year. The prospect of the two movements merging, perhaps with outbreaks of violence, poses a big challenge to the government -- and an opportunity for far-left and far-right presidential candidates jockeying for power.

item.title: India detains top 'cockroach' leader as hundreds protest in capital
item.description: Indian police detained Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leader Abhijeet Dipke on Friday ahead of fresh protests demanding the removal of the country's election chief, the youth-led movement said in a social media post. Dipke, 31, was detained shortly before a rally called by the online movement in the heart of New Delhi where hundreds of protesters marched on Friday evening, despite heavy security measures. FRANCE 24's Navodita Kumari reports from New Delhi, India.

item.title: Sean ‘Diddy’ Combs transferred to smaller US prison
item.description: Disgraced music producer Sean “Diddy” Combs, who was sentenced for prostitution-related crimes, has been transferred to a new US prison following media reports detailing an alleged brawl and special treatment behind bars. The 56-year-old was moved from the Fort Dix lockup in New Jersey to Allenwood Low in neighbouring Pennsylvania, a Bureau of Prisons spokeswoman told AFP on Friday. Both are low-security federal prisons for male offenders, but Allenwood Low has a population of around 1,000 compared to roughly 4,000 at Fort Dix. US media has reported that Combs was treated at a hospital for a head injury following a fight with another prisoner last weekend. And in September, NBC News reported that Combs enjoyed a relatively lavish lifestyle at Fort Dix, with access to contraband cellphones and liquor. The outlet also said Combs had men cooking and cleaning for him, as well as someone to give him Chinese-style massages. The Bureau of Prisons did not explain why Combs was transferred to the new prison. “For privacy, safety, and security reasons, we do not discuss the conditions of confinement for any individual in our custody, including reasons for transfer,” a spokeswoman said. Combs was sentenced in 2025 after a salacious trial that detailed the alleged “freak-offs” he organised: sexual marathons involving hired male escorts and his ex-girlfriend Casandra Ventura and another unidentified woman. He was acquitted by a jury of the most serious charges against him — sex trafficking and racketeering — but convicted of two counts of transporting people across state lines for prostitution. Combs is due to be released from prison in March 2028. AFP The post Sean ‘Diddy’ Combs transferred to smaller US prison appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: World’s Top Cocoa Producer Aims For A Climate-Tough Bean
item.description: Kofi Alexis Amani has watched the trees on his cocoa plantation wilt and sometimes wither as rains became unpredictable and less abundant in Côte d’Ivoire over the past several decades. “You can lose everything,” he sighed. The west African country is the world’s top cocoa producer, responsible for nearly 40 percent of global output. Its economy also depends on the crop, which accounts for 15 percent of GDP, supporting roughly five million people in a country of more than 33 million. So, scientists at the National Center for Agronomic Research (CNRA) have been working to develop a bean tough enough to survive the unpredictable weather events that man-made climate change has unleashed around the globe. Specifically, the researchers are working on bean varieties that are less sensitive to the availability of water. “We take the flowers from the male parents, which we then use to pollinate the flowers of the female parents… it’s their offspring that we take”, then test in the greenhouse and expose to various levels of water stress, geneticist Caudou Trebissou told AFP. So far, the researchers have come up with 11 “satisfactory” varieties, which they plan to eventually release on the market. Ivorian cocoa farmer Koffi Alexis Amani holds a cocoa pod at a plantation near Bouafle, on September 16, 2026.(Photo by ISSOUF SANOGO / AFP) Drier, hotter While rainfall has fluctuated in the country since the 1950s, it has steadily dropped since the 1980s, with the trend continuing over the past few decades, according to a report by the ministry of ecology. “From 2003 to 2022, we saw that rainfall has declined. We’re only at 1,100‑and‑something” millimetres of water on average per year in the region, instead of the 1,200 to 2,000 mm that cocoa trees need, Maryse Assi, a CNRA agronomist, said. When the plants manage to survive, “we see a drop in flowering or a shift in the flowering period” and “few fruits”, she added. The lack of rain also leads to “declines in soil fertility; some mineral elements will no longer be accessible to the plant”, she said. Farmers see this up close on their land. “When it doesn’t rain, the branches are dry, the leaves curl up” and “the pods are small”, said Anselme Kouakou, who grows cocoa a few kilometres from Amani in the centre of the country. A general view of pods on cocoa trees in a cocoa seed field belonging to the National Center for Agronomic Research (CNRA) near Divo, on September 15, 2026. (Photo by ISSOUF SANOGO / AFP) Future lies ‘in research’ While waiting for science to come up with a super-cocoa bean, Amani and others like him have tried to stem effects of climate change by altering how they plant their cocoa trees. He used to have just cocoa trees on his land. Now he intersperses them with cashew, iroko timber and banana — trees whose leaves shade the precious cocoa pods and whose trunks help irrigate them thanks to their high-water content. item.content:encoded: Kofi Alexis Amani has watched the trees on his cocoa plantation wilt and sometimes wither as rains became unpredictable and less abundant in Côte d’Ivoire over the past several decades. “You can lose everything,” he sighed. The west African country is the world’s top cocoa producer, responsible for nearly 40 percent of global output. Its economy also depends on the crop, which accounts for 15 percent of GDP, supporting roughly five million people in a country of more than 33 million. So far, the researchers have come up with 11 “satisfactory” varieties, which they plan to eventually release on the market. Ivorian cocoa farmer Koffi Alexis Amani holds a cocoa pod at a plantation near Bouafle, on September 16, 2026.(Photo by ISSOUF SANOGO / AFP) Drier, hotter While rainfall has fluctuated in the country since the 1950s, it has steadily dropped since the 1980s, with the trend continuing over the past few decades, according to a report by the ministry of ecology. “From 2003 to 2022, we saw that rainfall has declined. We’re only at 1,100‑and‑something” millimetres of water on average per year in the region, instead of the 1,200 to 2,000 mm that cocoa trees need, Maryse Assi, a CNRA agronomist, said. When the plants manage to survive, “we see a drop in flowering or a shift in the flowering period” and “few fruits”, she added. The lack of rain also leads to “declines in soil fertility; some mineral elements will no longer be accessible to the plant”, she said. Farmers see this up close on their land. “When it doesn’t rain, the branches are dry, the leaves curl up” and “the pods are small”, said Anselme Kouakou, who grows cocoa a few kilometres from Amani in the centre of the country. A general view of pods on cocoa trees in a cocoa seed field belonging to the National Center for Agronomic Research (CNRA) near Divo, on September 15, 2026. (Photo by ISSOUF SANOGO / AFP) Future lies ‘in research’ While waiting for science to come up with a super-cocoa bean, Amani and others like him have tried to stem effects of climate change by altering how they plant their cocoa trees. He used to have just cocoa trees on his land. Now he intersperses them with cashew, iroko timber and banana — trees whose leaves shade the precious cocoa pods and whose trunks help irrigate them thanks to their high-water content. The research cannot come fast enough in Côte d’Ivoire, predicted to be hit by extreme weather events like droughts or torrential rains in the coming decades. “The future of our orchards lies in research,” Yves Brahima Kone, who heads the cocoa industry’s regulatory body, said at the start of September. A general view of Sun-dried cofffe beans near Divo, on September 15, 2026. Ivory Coast is the world’s top cocoa producer, responsible for nearly 40 percent of global output. (Photo by ISSOUF SANOGO / AFP) Temperatures, which have already risen by 1C between 1991 and 2020 according to a government report, could continue to climb by 1.7C to 3.7C by 2080, according to studies. If nothing is done, “by 2050, Ivory Coast’s export agriculture will suffer a decline in cocoa production of 20 percent”, the government has warned. The country is not the only one likely to suffer — Europe, the world’s largest consumer of chocolate products, takes in 70 percent of Ivorian cocoa exports. item.title: [PHOTOS] Edo Gov Okpebholo Visits Oluku Market, Victims After Petrol Tanker Explosion
item.description: Edo State Governor, Senator Monday Okpebholo, has promised to rebuild Oluku Market, which was destroyed by fire, and support traders who lost their shops and goods in the incident. ﻿ Okpebholo gave the assurance on Friday after inspecting the damage at the market, located along the Benin-Lagos Road in Ovia North-East Local Government Area of the state. The governor said he was saddened by the incident, but noted that the disaster could have been avoided. Governor Monday Okpebholo criticised the owner of the affected tanker for bringing another tanker to transfer fuel without taking the necessary safety precautions. He assured the traders that his administration would not abandon them. He said the wife of the President, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, had expressed sympathy with the victims and the families of those who lost their lives. “I spoke to the First Lady this morning, and she expressed her sadness over what happened yesterday,” he was quoted as saying in a statement by his Chief Press Secretary, Patrick Ebojele. Governor Okpebholo urged residents to stay away from scenes of fire disasters involving petrol to prevent further casualties. “We are sorry. We, as human beings, should also take precautions whenever something like this happens. Before the explosion, people were scooping fuel. “But the state and federal governments have spent a lot of money on advertisements to educate the public to stay away from such disasters, but people won’t listen,” he said. Governor Monday Okpebholo criticised the owner of the affected tanker for bringing another tanker to transfer fuel without taking the necessary safety precautions. The governor also criticised the owner of the affected tanker for bringing another tanker to transfer the fuel without taking the necessary safety precautions. “The owner of the affected tanker also brought another tanker to evacuate the fuel, which is very wrong. If this had not happened, there would not have been any fire incident. “This is the result of it. We are sorry; it is not our making. We pray God keeps us alive,” he added. Governor Okpebholo also visited the burns and plastic ward of the Accident and Emergency Department, University of Benin Teaching Hospital (UBTH), where some victims were receiving treatment. Addressing the parents of the victims at the hospital, the governor reiterated the need for residents to heed safety warnings on the dangers of scooping fuel. He reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to rebuilding the market and helping the affected traders recover their livelihoods. item.title: The 7 Best Games to Play if You Loved Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave
item.description: It's been several weeks now since Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave was released for Nintendo Switch 2 , and fans around the world are still exploring this massive game. While you could easily sink hundreds of hours into playing through every Flame Lord's story, you may be wondering what to play after your adventures in Dagda are through. Worry not: we've compiled a list of our games like Fortune's Weave to keep your strategic skills sharp while you wait for Intelligent Systems to reveal their DLC plans.

item.title: Zelensky hails "real leaders" in Europe, blasts Trump's diesel deal with Russia
item.description: Ukrainian ​President Volodymyr Zelensky took aim on Friday at US President Donald Trump's diesel deal with Russia and welcomed the prospect of European allies stepping up their role in talks, calling Moscow's stance a "parody" of peace negotiations. At a European Union summit in Brussels, Zelenskiy said Russia did not want peace. He added that Ukraine was still experiencing disruptions to the SpaceX Starshield satellite system. FRANCE 24's Europe Editor Armen Georgian reports from Brussels.

item.title: Bellingham agrees new deal at Real Madrid
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Real Madrid midfielder Jude Bellingham has agreed a new five-year contract that would keep him at the club until 2031, Sky Sports reports, citing Spanish newspaper AS. The reported agreement would extend the England international’s current deal, which is due to expire in 2029. The 23-year-old is also expected to receive improved terms after negotiations began towards the end of last season. According to AS, Bellingham feels at home in Madrid, feels increasingly connected to Real Madrid and life in the Spanish capital, while the club’s supporters value his commitment and influence on the pitch. Since joining from Borussia Dortmund in 2023, Bellingham has emerged as a potential leader in a Real Madrid dressing room adjusting to the departures of influential figures such as Dani Carvajal, Luka Modrić and Toni Kroos. According to the report, the club are seeking a visible figurehead capable of taking on some of the leadership those veteran players provided. He joined Real from Borussia Dortmund in 2023 in a deal that could rise to £115 million. Since then, he has helped the Spanish club win the Champions League and LaLiga. Bellingham has scored three goals and provided three assists in eight league appearances this season, with Real now managed by Jose Mourinho, who took charge in the summer. Bellingham’s importance has grown under Mourinho, whose arrival has returned the midfielder to a role he is comfortable in: operating behind Kylian Mbappé with freedom to move across the pitch. The report also highlights his work without the ball, including initiating the press and contributing defensively. His performances at the World Cup have also strengthened his standing with England. After previously having difficulties under Thomas Tuchel, he has become a key player for the national side and scored eight goals at the tournament. The reported agreement for a new deal follows Vinicius Junior’s recent contract renewal. The Brazilian forward signed a new six-year deal after attracting interest from Arsenal in the summer. The post Bellingham agrees new deal at Real Madrid appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: France braces for massive protests: Yellow Vests to join students on Saturday
item.description: After weeks of student protests, France is set to be swept by broader, nationwide demonstrations on Saturday. The country's Yellow Vest movement – which eight years ago staged street protests against President Emmanuel Macron – has appealed to teachers, workers, pensioners and farmers, as well as students, in an online call spread through social media. The prospect of the two movements merging poses a big challenge to the government, as FRANCE 24’s Shirli Sitbon reports.

item.title: REPLAY: Ukraine's Zelensky holds presser in Brussels
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky on Friday urged European leaders to maintain their support for Kyiv and warned against easing sanctions on Russia. Speaking to reporters at the European summit in Brussels, Zelensky said that ending the war remained Ukraine’s priority but accused Russian President Vladimir Putin of having no genuine interest in negotiations. He also criticised a US deal involving Russian diesel, arguing that easing restrictions could allow Moscow to reap financial benefits and pave the way for broader sanctions relief. Watch the replay.

item.title: Nigeria had records of only 40,000 expatriates when we took over – Tunji-Ojo
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi Minister of Interior, Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, has disclosed that when he assumed office about three years ago, official records showed only about 40,000 expatriates working in Nigeria, a figure he said was impossible for a country of 200 million people. He spoke on Friday at the closing of a training on border control and immigration management for officers of the Nigeria Immigration Service NIS. “We got into a system where, by official records, we had maybe about 40,000 foreigners or whatever working in Nigeria. In a country of 200 million, that is not possible anywhere in the world. “And when you do not have the data of those foreigners residing in your country, then how do you manage their affairs? How do you monitor them? How do you monitor someone that you don’t even know exists?” He queried. Tunji-Ojo recalled that the ministry was then overseeing “an agency that should be technologically driven,” but “that wasn’t the case.” He said the ministry decided that “Nigeria cannot continue to be at the mercy of inefficiency.” According to him, the answer was to build what he called the Centralised Interior Management and Administration System, which is bringing the records of the correctional and fire services, and civil defence, into one portal. “Harmonisation of data, strategic handshake of data generating and processing agencies is the only way to have a single point of truth,” he said. He said the reform had ended the problem of multiple identities. “We had people then, one person with two, three different passports. But today, that is history,” he said. The minister said the NIS “of today is one of the most technologically advanced immigration services in the world.” He added that the ministry now has a 10-year technology roadmap and a data centre of “over eight petabytes,” which he described as one of the biggest in Africa, with its command and control centre running completely off-grid on solar power. Tunji-Ojo also had a warning for technology vendors. “Any vendor that is not ready to transfer knowledge to you has no place in the Ministry of Interior,” he said. Earlier, Comptroller General of the NIS, Kemi Nanna Nandap, said the Border Management Information System BMIS now holds over 15 million migration records, but “that number is not the achievement.” She told the graduating officers that technology would not replace their judgement. “An alert is not a verdict,” she said. Nandap set five standards for the officers, which she described as “non-negotiable”: accuracy, integrity, judgment, readiness and accountability. On integrity, she said: “Do not share your credentials. Do not search records out of curiosity. Never use this platform to grant favours, or to settle scores, or to facilitate improper passage. Any such abuse will be investigated and punished.” She said the programme would be judged by its results. “We will judge this programme by outcomes, not ceremonies,” Nandap said. item.title: Networking problems after the October 2026 Windows update? NTLM might be to blame
item.description: The October 2026 Windows security update may break networking for some customers who are still clinging to long-deprecated NTLMv1 security. A seemingly minor change in the update could have major implications for administrators and enterprises that haven't fully moved away from the legacy technology. Before the October 2026 update, Windows permitted NTLMv1-derived credentials for Single Sign-On and generated warning events. After the update, requests to use NTLMv1-derived credentials are blocked. It comes down to the BlockNtlmSSO registry value. If it hasn't been set, Windows will now use Enforce mode (1) instead of Audit mode (0), thus blocking requests and potentially impacting Wi-Fi, Ethernet, and VPN authentication, and therefore connections. The update does not set the value of BlockNtlmSSO, and administrators can set it to 0 to temporarily allow NTLMv1-derived Single Sign-On credentials. However, Microsoft noted, "Using Audit mode reduces the protection provided by Enforce mode and should only be considered as a scoped, temporary security exception." To be clear, this is not a bug and is by design. The addition of NTLM to the deprecation list occurred in 2024, and Microsoft added audit logs for NTLMv1 usage in late August 2025. The Windows giant has made no secret of its desire to ditch the legacy technology, stating in 2023, "Our end goal is eliminating the need to use NTLM at all." The problem is NTLM's longevity. It appeared in 1993 with Windows NT 3.1, and removing it from enterprise environments has proven tricky, even though it is somewhat insecure by modern standards. Microsoft removed it from Windows 11 24H2 and Windows Server 2025, but some remnants can still be found, notably when using MS-CHAPv2-based connections, including PEAP-MSCHAPv2, and EAP-MSCHAPv2, in a domain-joined environment. Hence the introduction of the audit mode in 2025, to help administrators spot where the technology was still being used. It is now 2026, and Microsoft has taken the next step. If Credential Guard is not enabled and BlockNtlmSSO is not set to Audit mode (0), the use of NTLMv1-derived credentials will be blocked as Microsoft works "to finalize the disablement of NTLMv1." There is no indication of how long the BlockNtlmSSO workaround (setting the value to Audit mode) will work - most likely until the next major Windows release. In September, Microsoft said, "In-market versions of Windows client and Windows Server will continue to support NTLM." However, it also stated, "Our long-term objective is a Windows platform that doesn't need NTLM at all." As such, if the message wasn't already clear, the move to enforce it by default makes it impossible to miss. The technology still exists in the operating system, but it is on its way out and will be removed in a future Windows release. Problems with networking after the October 2026 Windows security update could therefore signal that migration plans are not as far along, or as complete, as administrators mi

item.title: 5 iPhones that go head-to-head with Samsung’s top phones
item.description: Apple’s iPhones and Samsung continue to compete in the premium smartphone market, offering devices with advanced cameras, powerful processors, high-quality displays and artificial intelligence features. Samsung’s Galaxy S26 series competes directly with Apple’s Pro models, while Apple’s new foldable iPhone Duo introduces another challenger to Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold range. Here are five iPhones that go head-to-head with Samsung’s top smartphones. 1. iPhone 18 Pro Max The iPhone 18 Pro Max is Apple’s premium traditional smartphone, designed for users who want high performance, advanced photography and long battery life. Introduced in September 2026, it features Apple’s A20 Pro chip and a 48-megapixel main camera with variable aperture for greater control over photography. Apple also highlights improved battery life and sustained performance. Its main rival is the Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra, which offers a 200-megapixel main camera, advanced zoom capabilities, a 6.9-inch display and S Pen support. Both target users who want flagship performance, although Samsung places greater emphasis on long-range zoom and productivity tools. 2. iPhone 18 Pro The iPhone 18 Pro offers many of Apple’s premium features in a smaller package than the Pro Max. It is powered by the A20 Pro chip and features a 48-megapixel main camera with variable aperture, alongside improvements to battery life, cooling and camera controls. These features make it a strong option for users who want a high-end smartphone without choosing the largest model. Its closest Samsung competitor is the Galaxy S26+, which offers a 6.7-inch display, a 120Hz refresh rate and a triple-camera system with telephoto zoom. The iPhone appeals to users who prefer Apple’s iOS ecosystem, while Samsung offers Android flexibility and Galaxy AI tools. 3. iPhone Duo Apple’s iPhone Duo marks the company’s entry into the foldable smartphone market. Unveiled in September 2026, the device opens into a larger 7.6-inch display designed for multitasking and other screen-intensive activities. It also supports Apple Pencil input. Its most direct rival is Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold series. Samsung’s foldable phones have established themselves in the large-screen smartphone category, combining a conventional outer display with an expansive inner screen. The iPhone Duo gives Apple users a foldable option, while Samsung remains an established choice for those who want Android-based multitasking and foldable productivity features. 4. iPhone 17 Pro Max Although it is no longer Apple’s newest Pro Max model, the iPhone 17 Pro Max remains a premium alternative for buyers who do not necessarily need the latest generation. It features Apple’s A19 Pro chip and a high-end camera system, making it suitable for photography, video recording, gaming and demanding applications. Its main rival is the Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra. Samsung offers a more versatile zoom system and an integrated S Pen, while the iPhone is a strong option for users who p

item.title: Second term: Oyebanji vows to link education with jobs; Tinubu congratulates him
item.description: By Rotimi Ojomoyela President Bola Tinubu has congratulated the Governor of Ekiti State, Biodun Oyebanji on his inauguration for second term in office, urging him to consolidate on his previous achievements to deliver more dividends for the people of the state. Tinubu, represented by the Vice President, Senator Kashim Shettima at the inauguration ceremony in Ado-Ekiti, described Oyebanji’s victory as a testament of the trust that residents have in his administration and by extension, in the All Progressives Congress (APC). He further urged the residents to come en masse on January 16, 2026 and vote for President Bola Tinubu for a second term in office, in order to enjoy more dividends of democracy. Earlier in his speech, Governor Biodun Oyebanji pledged to prioritise electricity, agriculture, skills development, job creation and infrastructure in his second term, declaring that the success of his administration would be measured by the extent to which government investments improve the lives of ordinary citizens. Oyebanji said his administration would focus on translating infrastructure projects and public spending into tangible economic benefits for households, farmers, artisans, entrepreneurs and young people. The governor acknowledged the economic pressures confronting families, particularly the rising costs of food, transportation, education and other essential needs, stressing that government policies must deliver practical relief and expand opportunities for citizens. According to him, the prosperity his administration seeks must be reflected in better livelihoods, stronger businesses, productive farms, improved public services and greater economic security for families. He explained that roads should enable farmers to transport their produce to markets before harvests are lost, while reliable electricity should support industrialisation, improve productivity and help small businesses remain operational. The governor added that schools must equip children with knowledge, confidence and functional skills, while health facilities should provide accessible medical care without forcing families to exhaust their savings. Oyebanji said his administration would ensure that public expenditure was more closely linked to the everyday needs of residents, noting that development must enable people to earn better incomes, access essential services and plan their futures with greaterl confidence. On education and youth employment, the governor said his administration would strengthen the connection between formal education, practical skills and the demands of a changing economy. item.dc:creator: Henry Oduah
item.content:encoded: By Rotimi Ojomoyela President Bola Tinubu has congratulated the Governor of Ekiti State, Biodun Oyebanji on his inauguration for second term in office, urging him to consolidate on his previous achievements to deliver more dividends for the people of the state. Tinubu, represented by the Vice President, Senator Kashim Shettima at the inauguration ceremony in Ado-Ekiti, described Oyebanji’s victory as a testament of the trust that residents have in his administration and by extension, in the All Progressives Congress (APC). He further urged the residents to come en masse on January 16, 2026 and vote for President Bola Tinubu for a second term in office, in order to enjoy more dividends of democracy. Earlier in his speech, Governor Biodun Oyebanji pledged to prioritise electricity, agriculture, skills development, job creation and infrastructure in his second term, declaring that the success of his administration would be measured by the extent to which government investments improve the lives of ordinary citizens. Oyebanji said his administration would focus on translating infrastructure projects and public spending into tangible economic benefits for households, farmers, artisans, entrepreneurs and young people. The governor acknowledged the economic pressures confronting families, particularly the rising costs of food, transportation, education and other essential needs, stressing that government policies must deliver practical relief and expand opportunities for citizens. According to him, the prosperity his administration seeks must be reflected in better livelihoods, stronger businesses, productive farms, improved public services and greater economic security for families. He explained that roads should enable farmers to transport their produce to markets before harvests are lost, while reliable electricity should support industrialisation, improve productivity and help small businesses remain operational. The governor added that schools must equip children with knowledge, confidence and functional skills, while health facilities should provide accessible medical care without forcing families to exhaust their savings. Oyebanji said his administration would ensure that public expenditure was more closely linked to the everyday needs of residents, noting that development must enable people to earn better incomes, access essential services and plan their futures with greaterl confidence. On education and youth employment, the governor said his administration would strengthen the connection between formal education, practical skills and the demands of a changing economy. He described education as a defining part of Ekiti’s heritage, recalling the sacrifices made by parents who sold farm produce, postponed personal comfort and worked hard to ensure that their children received an education. “The measure of our second term will be how much of investment we have made improve the lives of our people,” he said, emphasising that roads, electricity, schools, airports and health facilities must serve clearly defined economic and social purposes. “In this second term, we will connect education more closely to enterprise, practical skills, and the need of a changing economy”. Oyebanji also pledged to expand agricultural productivity and strengthen the value chain by promoting processing, storage, packaging, transportation and marketing. He said land remained one of the state’s major economic assets, adding that government would work to ensure that farmers derived greater benefits from their labour. According to him, agricultural development requires coordinated investments in farm clusters, processing facilities, reliable electricity, water supply, transportation and access to capital. He said the administration wanted young people to view agriculture as a viable business capable of attracting knowledge, technology, investment and innovation, rather than merely as subsistence farming. The governor noted that opportunities extended beyond cultivation to other activities that could generate employment and retain more economic value within the state. “When agriculture prospers, the benefit travels from the farm to the market, from the market to the workshop, and from the workshop to the family home”. item.title: The risks faced by women migrants in Europe
item.description: This October marks 10 years since French police dismantled the notorious Calais "Jungle" camp. item.title: Mikel Arteta defends job cuts at Arsenal to help club ‘evolve and create success’
item.description: Up to 60 roles at risk after structural review Arteta signed new deal worth more than £20m a season Mikel Arteta has defended Arsenal’s decision to cut up to 60 jobs and insisted it was felt necessary to ensure they can continue achieving success. The Premier League champions are understood to have informed the staff whose positions are at risk after a consultation process started by Boston Consulting Group (BCG) before the end of last season. Arsenal hope the number of redundancies can be reduced and will attempt to redeploy affected employees wherever possible, although some job losses may be unavoidable. Continue reading...

item.title: A fake WhatsApp clone is showing up before the real version on the Play Store

As reported earlier by Android Authority , the WhatsApp dupe has racked up over 500,000 downloads and, at the time of writing, its Play Store listing is still live . Google did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The WhatsApp clone is from a developer going by "Agment Assets sallu" who doesn't currently have anything else listed on the Play Store. Their listing for the WhatsApp impostor has the same icon, screenshots, and text as the real version, but … Read the full story at The Verge.

item.title: 7 best places to see the northern lights, according to an aurora chaser
item.description: null I've spent years chasing the northern lights across the Arctic, from the mountains of Swedish Lapland to the dramatic Norwegian fjords. If there's one thing I've learned, it's that choosing where to see the northern lights is about much more than simply heading as far north as possible. Whether you're on the hunt for somewhere that offers the best chance of clear skies, the most dramatic scenery or a plethora of winter activities to keep you warm, choosing the right destination can make a big difference, especially as auroras are never guaranteed. My biggest piece of advice? Choose somewhere you've always wanted to visit regardless of whether the northern lights might appear. That way, the auroras become the icing on the cake rather than the sole measure of a successful trip. From my personal favorites in Scandinavia to some of North America's most established aurora hotspots, here are seven of the best places to see the northern lights this 2026/27 season. (Image credit: Daisy Dobrijevic) Best time to visit: September to early April Swedish Lapland holds a particularly special place in my heart. It's where I saw the northern lights for the very first time, during a trip to Kiruna in February 2023. I'd only booked two nights in Kiruna, one of which included a northern lights tour with Anders from Outdoor North 67º . Talk about putting all your eggs in one basket! But the gamble paid off, and I was treated to a spellbinding display of auroras dancing across the Arctic sky. I've been hooked ever since. Kiruna offers a wide range of accommodation, restaurants and activities, making it a convenient base for exploring the region. From here, you can join guided aurora tours, visit the famous Icehotel in Jukkasjärvi or head into the wilderness for dog sledding and snowmobiling adventures. item.dc:creator: Daisy Dobrijevic
item.content:encoded: null I've spent years chasing the northern lights across the Arctic, from the mountains of Swedish Lapland to the dramatic Norwegian fjords. If there's one thing I've learned, it's that choosing where to see the northern lights is about much more than simply heading as far north as possible. Whether you're on the hunt for somewhere that offers the best chance of clear skies, the most dramatic scenery or a plethora of winter activities to keep you warm, choosing the right destination can make a big difference, especially as auroras are never guaranteed. My biggest piece of advice? Choose somewhere you've always wanted to visit regardless of whether the northern lights might appear. That way, the auroras become the icing on the cake rather than the sole measure of a successful trip. From my personal favorites in Scandinavia to some of North America's most established aurora hotspots, here are seven of the best places to see the northern lights this 2026/27 season. Best places to see the northern lights at a glance Best places to see the northern lights at a glance Location Best for Kiruna and Abisko, Sweden Best for a short northern lights trip Tromsø, Norway Best for a city break Norwegian coast Best for a scenic Arctic voyage Finnish Lapland Best for a winter wonderland getaway Iceland Best for volcanoes, glaciers and natural wonders Fairbanks, Alaska Best for a U.S. aurora getaway Yellowknife, Canada Best for a Canadian aurora getaway Abisko and Kiruna, Sweden: Best for a short northern lights trip Northern lights from Mount Nuolja, Abisko, Sweden. (Image credit: Daisy Dobrijevic) Best time to visit: September to early April Swedish Lapland holds a particularly special place in my heart. It's where I saw the northern lights for the very first time, during a trip to Kiruna in February 2023. I'd only booked two nights in Kiruna, one of which included a northern lights tour with Anders from Outdoor North 67º . Talk about putting all your eggs in one basket! But the gamble paid off, and I was treated to a spellbinding display of auroras dancing across the Arctic sky. I've been hooked ever since. Kiruna offers a wide range of accommodation, restaurants and activities, making it a convenient base for exploring the region. From here, you can join guided aurora tours, visit the famous Icehotel in Jukkasjärvi or head into the wilderness for dog sledding and snowmobiling adventures. One of the region's biggest draws is Abisko National Park, around 60 miles (100 kilometers) northwest of Kiruna. Abisko is famous for its so-called "Blue Hole" , a local weather phenomenon in which the skies above the national park can be clear, even if the surrounding region (and weather forecast) is cloudy. This is partly thanks to the surrounding mountains, which create a rain shadow effect, reducing the precipitation in the area. Glacial-carved valley Lapporten, in Abisko National Park. (Image credit: Daisy Dobrijevic) And if you're visiting Abisko, I'd highly recommend taking the chairlift up Mount Nuolja to the Aurora Sky Station . The views across Abisko National Park and the surrounding mountains are spectacular. Just be sure to check the chairlift's operating dates and times before visiting, as it doesn't run throughout the entire season. My tip: Although my two-night gamble paid off, I wouldn't recommend relying on such a short window if seeing the northern lights is your main goal. If possible, give yourself at least three or four nights to improve your chances of clear skies and aurora activity. Tromsø, Norway: Best for a city break Tromsø is the perfect destination for an aurora city break. (Image credit: Juan Maria Coy Vergara via Getty Images) Best time to visit: September to early April If you want to experience the northern lights without giving up the comforts of city life, Tromsø is hard to beat. Located high above the Arctic Circle in northern Norway, Tromsø sits beneath the auroral oval, the region surrounding Earth's magnetic poles where auroras occur most frequently. What I particularly like about Tromsø is that it offers the best of both worlds. You have a lively city with excellent restaurants, cafes, shops, museums and accommodation, while spectacular mountains and wilderness are only a short journey away. There's also a huge range of northern lights tours available, from small-group photography excursions to longer aurora-chasing adventures. My tip: Tromsø is ideal if you want to combine northern lights hunting with a city break holiday. I'd recommend booking at least one guided aurora tour, particularly if the local weather forecast looks challenging. The Norwegian coast: Best for a scenic Arctic voyage Northern lights during a cruise along the Norwegian coast with Hurtigruten. (Image credit: Daisy Dobrijevic) Best time to visit: September to March If there's one northern lights experience I'd encourage people to consider, it's sailing along the Norwegian coast. I've been fortunate enough to travel along this extraordinary coastline on several occasions , and there's something very special about watching the northern lights from the deck of a ship, surrounded by good company, mountains, fjords and the dark Arctic sea. Operators such as Hurtigruten and HX offer voyages along the Norwegian coast, combining opportunities to see the northern lights with some of the most spectacular scenery in Europe. While Hurtigruten operates coastal voyages calling at towns and communities along the route, HX offers expedition-style experiences with a focus on exploring the natural environment. Arctic Norway during the winter months offers truly stunning views. Photo captured during a Hurtigruten voyage. (Image credit: Daisy Dobrijevic) Rather than staying in one location, you'll travel through different coastal landscapes, with opportunities to experience Arctic wildlife, local culture and winter excursions along the way. And then, of course, there's the possibility of the northern lights appearing overhead. Join me on a northern lights voyage! (Image credit: Daisy Dobrijevic) I'll be setting sail on a handful of Hurtigruten's astronomy voyages as a guest lecturer, sharing the science and wonder of the northern lights along the way. However, there's an important trade-off. Unlike a land-based aurora chase, a ship can't simply drive inland to escape coastal cloud cover. You're largely dependent on the weather along your route, although traveling through different regions over several nights gives you multiple opportunities. Hurtigruten also offers a Northern Lights Promise on qualifying voyages, providing a complimentary return voyage if the lights aren't officially sighted during your trip. Be sure to check the eligibility requirements and terms before booking. My tip: Choose a Norwegian coastal voyage because you want to experience the coastline itself. The scenery, communities and Arctic landscapes make it a remarkable journey regardless of auroras. Finnish Lapland: Best for a winter wonderland getaway Best time to visit: September to March If you dream of a northern lights holiday involving snow-covered forests, cozy cabins and perhaps even watching auroras from a glass-roofed igloo, Finnish Lapland could be the perfect choice. Northern Finland lies beneath the auroral oval, making it a popular destination for aurora chasers. Places such as Inari, Saariselkä and Ivalo offer excellent access to dark skies and Arctic wilderness. Rovaniemi, the official hometown of Santa Claus, is another popular option, particularly for families, although it's worth traveling away from the city's lights for the best views. My tip: For a quieter, more wilderness-focused escape, I'd look at northern Lapland around Inari or Saariselkä. If you're traveling with children or want a more activity-packed holiday, Rovaniemi may be a better fit.
