item.content:encoded: null Reentry and orbital-manufacturing provider Varda Space Industries is operating two spacecraft in orbit right now, with another expected to launch "in the coming days" and seven more next year. The Los Angeles-area startup, which bills itself as one of just two companies that can currently do commercial reentry from space, successfully launched its latest two refrigerator-sized spacecraft aboard SpaceX's Transporter-18 rideshare mission on Oct. 1. "It's humanity's first time launching multiple commercial reentry vehicles simultaneously," Varda CEO Will Bruey told Space.com on Tuesday (Oct. 7) of the Transporter-18 launch. The payloads on the Transporter-18 Varda craft ranged from pharmaceuticals to demo navigation systems to exterior thermal-protection materials. The company bills its spacecraft as mini-factories, which can host the orbital production of valuable goods such as pharmaceuticals and then bring them safely down to Earth. Another Varda vehicle is scheduled to follow them into space later this month. Assuming the third spacecraft launches nominally, all three will come down before Christmas in the Koonibba Test Range in the South Australian Outback, through coordination with Varda's long-time space-mission service provider, Southern Launch. And things are scheduled to ramp up quickly: Varda aims to fly seven more missions in 2027: two in Quarter 1 (Q1), two in Q2 and three in Q3 (the latter three being all on the same rocket). "As we scale up, we care about our ability to fly and fly regularly," Bruey said, emphasizing that the company is now treating its missions less as one-offs and more as a series. "It is, first and foremost, taking that unique [spacecraft] technology and moving into a fleet mentality, rather than a space mission mentality." One of Varda's reentry capsules is seen shortly after its touchdown in the Australian Outback. (Image credit: Varda Space/Rocket Lab) Like any startup finding its footing, Varda's challenges in the coming months will be scaling safely and efficiently. But the company says it is well-capitalized to do so, and has a big hiring campaign underway. It also has been spending money on slight upgrades and improvements to its vehicles, as well as mission operations and other infrastructure to run several missions at the same time, with more funds having just arrived. In September, Varda announced it had raised $251 million in "Series D" investment funding and will be hiring 100 people by the end of 2027, boosting its current 286-employee base by more than a third. Most of the employees work out of El Segundo, California, with a few in sales offices in Washington, D.C. and Huntsville, Alabama (where U.S. Space Command is gradually moving , along with some defense contractors, from Colorado Springs). In the further future, Bruey said, the goal is to fly Varda vehicles into space daily, using a "standardized product" that would be put together on an assembly line. But to get to that point, like other companies in the industry, Varda will need to get through an anticipated rocket shortage beginning in about 2029. SpaceX is by far the most active launcher these days, and it has been the dominant provider for companies like Varda via its Transporter and Bandwagon rideshare programs. But SpaceX is readying to retire its Falcon 9 rocket as it transitions more resources into Starship , the fully reusable megarocket the company sees as its workhorse of the future. Media reports suggest that SpaceX is pretty much out of capacity for Falcon 9 rockets flying through the end of service in 2028 or 2029, although slots are still available through third-party bookers. There are a slew of newer rockets under production (such as Blue Origin's New Glenn and Relativity Space's Terran R ), though they are far less mature and in some cases, even unflown. This is creating uncertainty about how much capacity there will be in the industry in the short term, but Varda said it is planning well ahead for that moment — and so too are its customers. "We're stacked with launches from now through that 2029 time frame," Bruey said. The company's current generation of vehicles is "launch-agnostic," although the next generation is aiming to be even more so to nab opportunities from small rockets up to Starship. The company said that, as long as Varda and its customers have access to microgravity , the shipping methodology — much like shipping on Earth — should not matter, and Varda aims to make the experience that seamless for its customers. But in the meantime, the company says it will fly as much as possible and (like everyone else) do what it can to secure slots on launching rockets after Falcon 9 retires.

item.title: Dettol Nigeria: Storytelling Wraps Up Challenge with 30 Winners
item.description: Dettol Nigeria has concluded its “12 Hour Protective Shield” storytelling challenge, recognizing 30 Nigerians for sharing personal stories about their experiences with Dettol Original Antibacterial Bar Soap. The Dettol Original 12hrs Protection Challenge ran from 13 July to 31 August 2026, and invited Nigerians to share personal Dettol stories ranging from childhood memories to family and personal hygiene routines. After the challenge closed, 30 winners were selected and rewarded with cash prizes for their entries. The challenge was part of the wider campaign for Dettol Original Soap, built around its 12-hour protective shield against 99.9% of illness-causing germs. Under the campaign idea, “ 12 Hours, Protection That Moves With You, ” Dettol highlighted the importance of consistent hygiene as people move through their daily activities. Beyond the digital campaign, Dettol brought the experience directly to consumers through in market activations across multiple states in Nigeria, combining product education and demonstrations with handwashing stations and consumer engagement. Commenting on the campaign, Boma Harrison , Marketing Director, Reckitt West Africa , said, “We were particularly pleased to give Nigerians the opportunity to share their personal Dettol stories and hear what protection means to them and their families. The stories shared through the challenge reflect the place Dettol has held in Nigerian households over the years, while reinforcing the importance of hygiene in everyday life. ” The campaign brought together digital storytelling, consumer engagement and on-ground experiences to reinforce Dettol Original’s role in everyday hygiene routines, while giving Nigerians an opportunity to share the personal experiences that have shaped their connection with the brand. item.title: Fashion Innovation Africa to Convene 300+ Stakeholders at Inaugural Conference in Lagos on October 22
item.description: Fashion Innovation Africa (FIA) 2026 will bring together more than 300 stakeholders from across fashion, finance, technology and government to examine the structures, investments and partnerships needed to build a stronger and globally competitive African fashion industry. Scheduled for Thursday, October 22, 2026, at Landmark Event Centre, Victoria Island, Lagos, the inaugural business conference is themed “From the Atelier to the Economy: The Architecture Behind African Fashion”. Endorsed by the Lagos State Government, FIA 2026 will focus on the systems and capabilities required to translate Africa’s creative talent into sustainable businesses, jobs and wider economic opportunities. The conference will convene successful fashion founders and business leaders alongside representatives from government, regulatory agencies, financial institutions, technology companies, logistics providers and other stakeholders across the fashion value chain. By bringing these groups together, FIA aims to strengthen connections between the creative, commercial and institutional players whose collaboration is essential to the industry’s growth. The full-day programme will feature a Government Keynote, fireside chats with leading founders, three panel discussions and concurrent masterclasses. Discussions will address critical industry issues, including access to growth capital, local manufacturing, supply chain resilience, quality standards, technology, trade frameworks and access to international markets. Uche Ajene , Convener of Fashion Innovation Africa, said the conference draws inspiration from the growth of Nigeria’s music and film industries, which have built stronger commercial structures and expanded their global reach over time. “There was a time when Nigerian music and Nollywood had immense talent but were still building the structures needed to support their growth and global reach. Today, both have made significant strides in taking Nigerian creativity to the world,” she said. “African fashion has similar potential, but realising it requires more than talent and visibility. We need stronger systems for financing, production, distribution, standards and market access. FIA is bringing the key players together to help build that architecture and position African fashion for sustainable growth and global competitiveness.” Beyond the conference programme, FIA 2026 will provide opportunities for businesses and industry stakeholders to showcase solutions, exchange ideas, build strategic partnerships and explore commercial opportunities across the fashion value chain. Fashion Innovation Africa is an initiative focused on strengthening Africa’s fashion ecosystem by connecting the people, businesses and institutions that shape its growth. Through industry convenings, strategic collaborations and opportunities for knowledge exchange, FIA seeks to advance the infrastructure, investment and market access needed to build a more connected, commercially sustainable and

item.title: 'Space Gal' Emily Calandrelli launches into the Marvel Universe this week on Disney Jr.'s 'Iron Man' series (exclusive)
item.description: null "The Space Gal" is blasting off onto her next adventure to promote STEM education with out-of-this-world content. Science communicator and citizen astronaut Emily Calandrelli, better known to millions of social media followers as "The Space Gal," is bringing her real-world spaceflight experience to the Marvel universe . Calandrelli is lending her voice to an upcoming episode of Disney Jr.'s animated series, "Marvel's Iron Man and his Awesome Friends." She is stepping into the role of a character called Astronaut Amy in the episode "The Iron Friends in Space," offering another opportunity for Calandrelli to share her enthusiasm for space with younger audiences. Astronaut Amy meets characters on "Marvel's Iron Man and his Awesome Friends." (Image credit: Disney) Calandrelli is an engineer, author and television host whose career has focused on making complex scientific concepts engaging and accessible. Growing from her online presence as @TheSpaceGal , Calandrelli has produced numerous educational videos, books and television appearances, including a role on the Netflix "Bill Nye the Science Guy" revival series, "Bill Nye Saves the World." In a preview clip provided exclusively to Space.com by Disney, Calandrelli's character is welcomed by Tony Stark, Riri Williams, Amadeus Cho and Vision as they explore a moon-themed museum display. The exhibit features a holographic model of the moon and other space-themed artifacts, providing a backdrop for Astronaut Amy to share information about space and lunar exploration. The show follows younger versions of Stark and others from Marvel's familiar superhero roster, as they navigate conflicts that are scaled down from the franchise's world-ending blockbuster emergencies to more age-appropriate problem-solving and teamwork-building storylines. Calandrelli's cameo puts her alongside characters already rich in their storylines with backgrounds in science and technology, like Stark and Williams, known by their alter egos Iron Man and Ironheart, both of whose superhero identities revolve around the mastery of sophisticated technology and engineering. And while Astronaut Amy and her super co-stars live in Marvel's fictional universe, Calandrelli's inclusion in the episode creates the opportunity to introduce some real-life scientific concepts. Her appearance also comes as Disney prepares to expand the animated series to include a larger ensemble. Beginning next summer, the show will evolve into "Marvel's Avengers: Mightiest Friends", and bring additional characters into the fold, including Captain America, Hulk, Black Panther, Black Widow and Thor, according to Disney. For Calandrelli, the role represents another extension of a career dedicated to making space exploration relatable and exciting for the next generation. And while Astronaut Amy and her super co-stars live in Marvel's fictional universe, Calandrelli's inclusion in the episode creates the opportunity to introduce some real-life scientific concepts. Her appearance also comes as Disney prepares to expand the animated series to include a larger ensemble. Beginning next summer, the show will evolve into "Marvel's Avengers: Mightiest Friends", and bring additional characters into the fold, including Captain America, Hulk, Black Panther, Black Widow and Thor, according to Disney. For Calandrelli, the role represents another extension of a career dedicated to making space exploration relatable and exciting for the next generation. In November 2024, Calandrelli became the 100th woman to reach space when she launched aboard Blue Origin 's New Shepard rocket on the company's NS-28 suborbital mission. The flight carried her above the Kármán line , the internationally recognized boundary of space, and gave her several minutes of weightlessness before the capsule and its crew returned to Earth . Calandrelli isn't the first real-life astronaut to lend her voice to the Marvel universe. Former NASA astronaut and the first Black woman in space Mae Jemison guest-starred in Disney's "Marvel's Moon Girl and Devil Dinosaur" in March 2023. Jemison voiced a fictional app called Skipster, created by the show's young superhero and scientific prodigy, Lunella Lafayette. Another space traveler, citizen astronaut Kellie Gerardi, also just announced over the weekend (Oct. 12) her cast credit in the upcoming movie "Hexed", from Disney's Animation Studios. Viewers can catch the upcoming episode of "Marvel's Iron Man and his Awesome Friends," titled, "The Iron Friends in Space," during its Disney Jr. premiere on Oct. 14 or streaming on Disney+ beginning Oct. 28. item.title: Companies rushed in on AI. Now some are pulling back
item.description: Rapid AI adoption left workers cleaning up a flood of errors and low-quality work Employers around the globe are grappling with the fallout from rushing to adopt fast-changing artificial intelligence tools. Meta has scaled back plans to axe staff and use more AI agents after the company found employees were spending more and more time cleaning up technical and security errors, Reuters reported . And after thinning its workforce, especially middle managers , in a 2023 efficiency push, the company is expanding its managerial ranks again, LinkedIn posts from workers show. Continue reading...

item.title: Desperados and Young Jonn Create a Cross-Cultural Anthem For Living In The Moment With ‘Let It Go’
item.description: From the infectious rhythms of Latin music to the unmistakable pulse of Afrobeats, Desperados and Young Jonn are bringing two cultures together on “Let It Go, ” a new track inspired by living in the moment. Some moments are best enjoyed without overthinking them: a spontaneous night out, an unexpected link-up with friends, or the song that gets everyone moving. Capturing this spirit of freedom and self-expression, Desperados has teamed up with award-winning Afrobeats producer, songwriter and artist Young Jonn for “Let It Go.” Produced by Yung Willis , the Grammy-nominated music producer whose production credits span some of the biggest names in African music. Having worked with notable artistes including Falz, Wizkid, Kizz Daniel, Davido, Niniola, BNXN, Zlatan, Patoranking and Ice Prince , Yung Willis brings his production expertise to the collaboration, helping shape a sound that connects global influences with the energy of Afrobeats. Rooted in the brand’s identity and association with self-expression, Desperados continues to find meaningful ways to connect with the younger audience through music, culture and premium experiences. With “Let It Go”, the brand is using music as a touchpoint between its Latin roots and the energy of Nigerian culture. At the heart of the collaboration is “ Guao Guao ,” the reggaeton track Desperados created in partnership with Venezuelan artist Micro TDH and Colombian producer Ovy On The Drums. Built around a sample of this unique record, Let It Go brings a Latin-inspired sound into Young Jonn’s style, creating an Afrobeats song that reflects Nigeria’s vibrant music and nightlife culture. “Let It Go” is more than a fusion of two sounds. It is an expression of the Desperados vibe, where music becomes a way to encourage people to loosen up and enjoy moments that make life memorable. By connecting the global influence of Latin music with Afrobeats, the brand reinforces its place through music, culture, and self-expression. Young Jonn’ s ability to reinterpret global influences through a distinctive Nigerian style makes him a fitting partner for this expression. Rather than recreating the original, he gave the sound a fresh identity, shaped by the rhythm and movement of Nigerian music. Whether it’s the rhythm that takes over the dance floor, an ordinary link-up that turns into a memorable experience, the song captures the freedom of letting go and being fully in the moment. For Desperados, the brand’s involvement gives the song a cultural expression, connecting its identity to a sound that brings people together, encourages movement and creates room for memories. From recreating dance moves to sharing interpretations through lifestyle content, fans can join the “Let It Go” vibe beyond simply listening. Watch the official music video below Listen to “Let It Go” here . Ready to catch the vibe? Follow @desperadosng for more updates. item.title: Mark Your Calendars! Ecclesia Hills Church Announces 6th Ecclesia Word Conference, “Freedom in Christ”
item.description: Ecclesia Hills Church is pleased to announce the sixth edition of the Ecclesia Word Conference, themed “Freedom in Christ.” The conference will take place from Friday, 6th November to Sunday, 8th November 2026, at The Hall, 16 Musa Yar’adua Street, Victoria Island . The Ecclesia Word Conference has grown into a gathering where believers are taught, equipped, and stirred to live out the fullness of their faith. Last year’s edition explored the theme Custodian of Holy Oracles . This year’s edition turns to a question at the heart of the Gospel: What is freedom in Christ, and how can the Ecclesia arrive there? “This conference is crucial to bringing believers to the accuracy of freedom,” said Pastor Moses Ida-Michaels , Pastor of Ecclesia Hills Church. “Many people carry the name of Christ yet remain bound by religion, fear, habits, financial pressure, and generational patterns. This gathering is about seeing freedom clearly and walking in it. Together, we will hack the principles that bring true liberty to life,” he concluded. Conference Focus Across three days, sessions will address freedom in every area of life, including: Free a Generation: El-Shakar Freedom from Religion: Jabar Mckellar Freedom from Mammon: Chris Delvan Freedom in Illumination: Eva Dan Yusuf Freed Bloodlines, Cycles, Enchantments: Edem Julius-Cudjoe Freedom from Sinful Addictions / Fear of Consequence: Chris Delvan Free to Serve God’s Purpose: Chris Delvan Freedom in Innovation / Innovative Liberty: Moses Ida-Michaels (Host Pastor) Liberty Ideology: Edem Julius-Cudjoe Worship will be led by Hill Music and Moses Akoh , creating an atmosphere for encounter, response, and transformation. Event Details Event: Ecclesia Word Conference 2026 (6th Edition) Theme: Freedom in Christ Dates: Friday, 6th November to Sunday, 8th November 2026 Venue: The Hall, 16 Musa Yar’adua Street, Victoria Island, Lagos Schedule: Friday: 9:00 AM Saturday: 8:00 AM Sunday: 12:00 PM Admission: Free Registration (Required): Register Here Host: Ecclesia Hills Church Sponsored Content The post Mark Your Calendars! item.title: More Than Just a Glass of Milk: A Dietitian’s Perspective on Why Milk Matters
item.description: If you grew up in Nigeria in the 90s or early 2000s, chances are you didn’t learn about milk from a science class. You learnt about it from television. Back then, adverts were part of our childhood. We didn’t reach for a remote every time the commercials came on. We sang the jingles, quoted the catchphrases and years later, many of us can still remember them word for word. For me, one advert stands above the rest. It followed a young Kanu Nwankwo as he dribbled a football through the dusty streets of Owerri on an errand for his mother. He left home with nothing but a football at his feet, dribbling all the way to the market. Just as a tin of milk slipped from the market woman’s hands, he flicked it back into the air with effortless skill. She smiled and said, “Papilo, I know say one day you go make us proud.” As children, we believed her. Not because we understood marketing, but because those adverts made us believe that greatness could begin anywhere. They told us that a boy from Owerri, Nigeria could become one of Africa’s greatest footballers. They told us that ordinary children with big dreams could grow into extraordinary adults. And somewhere between that advert and my mum pouring Milk into my breakfast cereal every morning before school, I came to believe two things. The first was that milk helped build strong bones and teeth. The second was that maybe, just maybe, I could become whoever I dreamed of becoming. Years later, after becoming a dietitian, I realised that my childhood understanding wasn’t wrong, it was simply incomplete. Today, conversations about milk have become surprisingly complicated. Social media is filled with conflicting opinions. Some people insist milk is only for children. Others believe it causes weight gain. Some assume all milk is the same, while others believe dairy milk and non- dairy offer identical nutrition. As nutrition professionals, we know that the truth is rarely found in headlines or viral videos. It is found in evidence. So, let’s separate what we know about milk from what we only think we know. item.content:encoded: If you grew up in Nigeria in the 90s or early 2000s, chances are you didn’t learn about milk from a science class. You learnt about it from television. Back then, adverts were part of our childhood. We didn’t reach for a remote every time the commercials came on. We sang the jingles, quoted the catchphrases and years later, many of us can still remember them word for word. For me, one advert stands above the rest. It followed a young Kanu Nwankwo as he dribbled a football through the dusty streets of Owerri on an errand for his mother. He left home with nothing but a football at his feet, dribbling all the way to the market. Just as a tin of milk slipped from the market woman’s hands, he flicked it back into the air with effortless skill. She smiled and said, “Papilo, I know say one day you go make us proud.” As children, we believed her. Not because we understood marketing, but because those adverts made us believe that greatness could begin anywhere. They told us that a boy from Owerri, Nigeria could become one of Africa’s greatest footballers. They told us that ordinary children with big dreams could grow into extraordinary adults. And somewhere between that advert and my mum pouring Milk into my breakfast cereal every morning before school, I came to believe two things. The first was that milk helped build strong bones and teeth. The second was that maybe, just maybe, I could become whoever I dreamed of becoming. Years later, after becoming a dietitian, I realised that my childhood understanding wasn’t wrong, it was simply incomplete. Today, conversations about milk have become surprisingly complicated. Social media is filled with conflicting opinions. Some people insist milk is only for children. Others believe it causes weight gain. Some assume all milk is the same, while others believe dairy milk and non- dairy offer identical nutrition. As nutrition professionals, we know that the truth is rarely found in headlines or viral videos. It is found in evidence. So, let’s separate what we know about milk from what we only think we know. What Exactly Is Milk? From a scientific perspective, milk is the natural nutrient-rich fluid produced by mammals to nourish their young during the earliest stages of life. For humans, cow’s milk is the most widely consumed form of dairy milk and has been part of diets around the world for generations. But from a nutrition perspective, milk is much more than its definition. It is a naturally nutrient-dense food that provides a unique combination of high-quality protein, calcium, phosphorus, vitamin B12, riboflavin and other essential nutrients that work together to support growth, bone health, muscle function, energy production and overall wellbeing throughout life. Unlike many foods that contribute just one or two key nutrients, milk delivers several essential nutrients in one convenient food. This is one of the reasons it has remained a staple in many cultures and continues to play an important role in healthy eating patterns across different stages of life. Yet despite these nutritional benefits, milk remains one of the most misunderstood foods on our tables. Over the years, I’ve heard people say that milk is only for children, that it causes weight gain or that all milk products are the same. Social media has only amplified these conversations, making it increasingly difficult to separate evidence from opinion. So, let’s look at some of the most common myths about milk and what science tells us. Why Milk Matters One of the things I have learned after years of working as a dietitian is that conversations about milk often focus on just one nutrient: calcium. Yes, milk is well known for supporting strong bones and healthy teeth, but that’s only one part of the story. Milk provides a unique combination of nutrients that work together to support the body in different ways. Rather than contributing just one benefit, it supplies several essential nutrients in a single food, each playing its own role in maintaining good health. High-quality protein helps build and repair muscles, organs and other body tissues. It’s essential for growth in children and helps adults maintain muscle mass throughout life. Calcium and phosphorus work together to support strong bones and healthy teeth. These nutrients are especially important during childhood and adolescence, when bones are developing rapidly, but they also remain important throughout adulthood to help maintain bone health. Vitamin B12 plays an essential role in the production of healthy red blood cells and supports the normal functioning of the nervous system. Riboflavin (vitamin B2) helps the body convert the food we eat into the energy we need for everyday activities. Many Milk products are also fortified with vitamins A and D. Vitamin A supports healthy vision and the normal functioning of the immune system, while vitamin D helps the body absorb calcium effectively, making it an important partner in maintaining strong bones. What makes milk unique isn’t that it contains one remarkable nutrient. It’s that it brings many important nutrients together in one food. That combination is one of the reasons milk has remained part of healthy dietary patterns across different cultures and generations. A glass of Milk doesn’t provide just one nutrient. It provides a package of nutrients working together to support growth, development and overall wellbeing. Myth 1: “Milk Is Only for Children” One of the most common misconceptions I hear is that milk is something we eventually outgrow, that once we become adults, it no longer has a place in our diet. I understand where that idea comes from. Many of us first encountered milk as children. It was stirred into our morning pap, added to cereal before school or mixed into a warm cup of tea on rainy days. Over time, it’s easy to begin thinking of milk as a “children’s food.” But our bodies tell a different story. While our nutritional needs change throughout life, they never stop. In fact, the nutrients milk provides continue to support us in different ways as we grow older. For children, milk contributes high-quality protein, calcium and other essential nutrients that support healthy growth and the development of strong bones and teeth. During the teenage years, when growth accelerates and nutritional demands increase, these nutrients remain just as important. As adults, the focus shifts. Growth may slow, but maintaining muscle mass, preserving bone health and meeting our daily nutrient needs become priorities. The high-quality protein, calcium and other vitamins and minerals found in milk continue to contribute to those goals as part of a balanced diet. For older adults, maintaining muscle strength and bone health becomes increasingly important. Adequate protein helps preserve muscle as we age, while calcium and vitamin D, where milk is fortified with vitamin D, continue to support healthy bones. In other words, milk doesn’t stop being relevant because we grow older, its role simply changes. The nutrients remain valuable. What changes is how our bodies use them at different stages of life. Perhaps that’s a better way to think about it. Milk grows with us, not because every person must drink milk every day, but because the nutrients it provides continue to support health from childhood through older adulthood as part of a healthy, balanced diet. Myth 2: “Milk Causes Weight Gain” If you’ve spent any time on social media, you’ve probably come across someone confidently declaring that milk is “too fattening” or should be avoided if you’re trying to manage your weight. It’s a message that’s repeated so often that many people now accept it as fact. The reality, however, is much less dramatic. No single food causes weight gain on its own. Weight gain occurs when, over time, we consistently consume more energy than our bodies use. Overall dietary patterns, portion sizes, physical activity, sleep and othe

item.title: adidas x waf. Superstar ADV Brings Lagos Skate Culture to the Global Stage
item.description: On Monday, 12 October 2026, adidas and waf. (Wflsncrm ) release the Superstar ADV worldwide, marking the first time an African skate community has shaped the silhouette since its 1970 debut. Co-established in 2012 by Jomi Marcus-Bello, Nifemi Marcus-Bello, and KC Obijiaku, waf. has spent 14 years nurturing the Lagos skateboarding scene from the ground up, culminating in the opening of a skatepark at Freedom Park, located on the site of a former colonial prison, in 2024. This rich heritage is directly integrated into the sneaker’s aesthetic, featuring a dusty grey upper inspired by Lagos Island, breathable side panels crafted for the climate of Lagos, and a translucent pink outsole designed to evoke the city’s horizon at distinct moments of the day. The release begins at the waf. flagship in Lagos and across all adidas retail and e-commerce platforms worldwide at $110. Launch time at the Lagos flagship: 9:00 a.m. WAT. ABOUT WAF. waf. (Wafflesncream) is Nigeria’s pioneering skate community and the first hub for skate culture in West Africa, combining a retail space with a creative community. For fourteen years, it has grown Lagos’ skate scene through community programming, retail, fashion, and music. In 2017, waf. launched Nigeria’s first Go Skate Day, now one of the country’s largest annual skate festivals. ABOUT ADIDAS ORIGINALS Inspired by the rich sporting heritage of adidas, one of the world’s leading sports brands and a global designer and developer of athletic footwear and apparel, adidas Originals is a lifestyle brand founded in 2001. With the adidas archive at its foundation, adidas Originals continues to evolve the brand’s legacy through its commitment to product innovation and its ability to filter the creativity and courage found on the courts and sporting arenas through the lens of contemporary youth culture. BellaNaija is a Media Partner for adidas x waf. Superstar ADV The post adidas x waf. Superstar ADV Brings Lagos Skate Culture to the Global Stage appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. Read today! .

item.title: NASA's Perseverance Mars rover breaks interplanetary driving record — and it's far from done
item.description: null In a milestone achievement, NASA's Perseverance Mars rover has broken the record for most miles driven on a world beyond Earth. On Oct. 11, Perseverance hit 28.10 miles (45.22 kilometers) traveled on Mars, breaking the record previously held by NASA's Opportunity rover which went 28.06 miles (45.16 km). It took Oppy 14 years to cover all that ground; Perseverance, by contrast, has been on Mars for just 5.5 years. The new record is far from the end of Perseverance's journey, however; the mission team thinks the rover could eventually more than double the distance it's already traveled. "Our original design was only planned to last for [about] 20 kilometers of driving," Mark Maimone, a rover driver at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) in Southern California, told Space.com . Perseverance has set a new off-world record! 🏅On Oct. 11, the rover's odometer hit 28.10 miles (45.22 kilometers), eclipsing the distance record set by NASA's Opportunity rover. 1/2 https://t.co/IThlI7dl2z October 12, 2026 "We've more than doubled that already … and we're looking really good to go for up to 100 kilometers total," added Maimone, who works as a designated principal in autonomous planetary rover navigation on Perseverance and helped to develop the autonomous driving systems on NASA's previous Mars rovers. "So we could double what we've done so far," he said. "And we have great expectations that [Perseverance] can continue its mission of exploring and collecting really useful and beneficial samples that will tell us so much more about the history of Mars." Indeed, Perseverance remains in great shape, mission team members stressed. "We are very fortunate that all of Perseverance's original capabilities are more or less intact, especially for the science instruments," JPL's Vivian Sun, the mission's deputy project scientist, told Space.com. Perseverance landed on the floor of Mars' 28-mile-wide (46 km) Jezero Crater in February 2021. It was far from the first robot to traverse the planet's surface; the Perseverance team built on years of experience with the Sojourner, Spirit, Opportunity and Curiosity rovers. Through the triumphs and missteps of these previous craft, NASA learned how to better explore another planet with a rover operated from millions of miles away. Perseverance saw massive improvements made to everything from its specialty wheels to its autonomous driving system and onboard tools and instruments. This "could not have been done without the previous missions that we've sent to Mars," Sun said. "Five years later [after landing], we're definitely a very well oiled machine," she added. "There's a lot of technical advancements on Perseverance that are the result of many people, many engineers, working on this new technology year after year for decades now." And, according to both Sun and Maimone, this teamwork is the real secret behind Perseverance's endurance and success. "The magic sauce for our operations team is how cohesively we work togeth

And, according to both Sun and Maimone, this teamwork is the real secret behind Perseverance's endurance and success. "The magic sauce for our operations team is how cohesively we work together," Sun said. The engineers, rover drivers and science team all work together and keep each other's work in mind as they make decisions on everything from driving speed to science targets, she added. "I'm just super appreciative of all the people that have and still work on the mission. They're really what makes the mission special," Sun said. What's next for Perseverance As the team mentioned, Perseverance is nowhere near done on Mars. The rover could keep driving for many more miles on the Red Planet, and the scientists and engineers at NASA have big plans and high hopes for its future. "We are currently planning to continue down south on the crater rim," Sun said. "There's a whole diversity of different rocks along this crater rim going south that we want to investigate and figure out how it indicates conditions from early Mars." Jezero is a giant crater created by an impact from an asteroid or comet billions of years ago. Perseverance's work has shown that Jezero hosted a lake for long stretches billions of years ago. Scientists are therefore eager to continue exploring the site, searching for clues about what the planet looked like in the ancient past, and if it could have possibly hosted life . "There are huge chunks of pre-Jezero crust that were embedded in the stratigraphy or got thrown up by the impact, and they're now incorporated onto the crater rim," Sun said. "These are our chance to probe like really old rocks that don't really exist in any other form on the surface anymore." As part of Perseverance's next steps south on the crater rim, the team is heading toward an area called "Rainbow Falls." Sun said that the Rainbow Falls area is thought to have kaolinite, a clay mineral that forms when water interacts with rock. By studying these types of minerals, mission scientists might be able to get a better idea of the conditions on Mars all of those billions of years ago, when water filled Jezero Crater. "Whenever we are looking at clay minerals, I think the question of habitability and the search for potential biosignatures is always on the table," Sun said. "So that is very much the case when we get to Rainbow Falls, or even when we see kaolinite."

item.title: The biggest threat from AI is the sense that we have no say in it. To that I say game on | Peter Lewis
item.description: The tech bros and their highly paid sock puppets are banking on us giving in to their ‘inevitability doctrine’. But in Australia, and around the world, resistance is rising Of all the drivers of the populist wave, one of the most powerful is the sense of inevitability that surrounds what we are told is the march of progress. In presenting the future as a fait accompli, it poisons the civic well by dealing us out of the game. While the US clings on to its status as the oldest constitutional democracy, the unholy alliance between the tech overlords and the White House is creating its own AI reality untethered to the will of the people . Continue reading...

item.title: Astronaut captures mesmerizing auroras with iPhone from ISS | Space photo of the day for Oct. 13, 2026
item.description: null Earth's night side is wreathed in colorful auroras in a new smartphone image captured from the ISS. (Image credit: Anil Menon, NASA) NASA astronaut Anil Menon captured a gorgeous view of the northern lights dancing over the night side of Earth from the International Space Station on Oct. 10 using an iPhone camera. What is it? Menon's photo reveals spectacular pink, purple and red auroras glowing in Earth's upper atmosphere above a sparse dappling of city lights, subtly blurred by the motion of the orbital spacecraft over the course of the exposure. Bright stars glimmer between the solar panels and outer hulls of the ISS and visiting spacecraft, painted purple by the auroral display. "Flying through is rare and amazing," Menon wrote in a separate aurora video he posted to X on Oct. 10. "You can see the lights on the outside of [the] station reflecting back like Christmas LEDs. It's definitely more immersive." Why is it amazing? Menon captured the auroras during a period of heightened geomagnetic activity, after several coronal mass ejections (CMEs) struck Earth's magnetic field, triggering geomagnetic storms ranging from minor (G1) to strong (G3) over the weekend. During geomagnetic storms, more charged particles are accelerated along Earth's magnetic field lines toward the polar regions, where they collide with gases in the upper atmosphere; they excite them, causing them to release energy as light and producing spectacular auroral displays. The blue-purple colors seen in Menon's image are largely produced by nitrogen at altitudes of around 60-120 miles (100-200 kilometers) , while the red hue comes from oxygen atoms higher up, typically above 125 miles (200 kilometers). The photo is particularly impressive because it was captured on an iPhone camera, as opposed to the more traditional Nikon cameras that astronauts sometimes use to capture Earth during their time aboard the ISS. Smartphone astrophotography has become increasingly popular over recent years, with some models now featuring bespoke modes for capturing the night sky. iPhones were even used by the astronauts of the Artemis 2 mission to document their historic flyby of the moon earlier this year! Interested in capturing your own images of the night sky using your mobile phone? Then be sure to check out our guide to photographing stars, the moon and the Milky Way with nothing but your smartphone camera.

item.title: Emir of Kano to Lead Sustainability Leaders at STS’ 10-Year Milestone in Lagos
item.description: With four years remaining to the 2030 Sustainable Development Goals deadline, the Sustainability Table Discourse Series (STS) will mark its tenth anniversary on 15–16 October 2026 at the Balmoral Convention Centre, Federal Palace Hotel, Victoria Island, Lagos, with a deliberate shift from dialogue to delivery. Under the theme ‘Leading the Sustainable Development Agenda: People, Planet and Prosperity,’ STS @10 will bring together leaders from government, business, finance, development institutions, technology and civil society to address a defining question: how can Africa bridge the gap between sustainable development ambition and execution? Headlining the gathering is H.H. Muhammadu Sanusi II , Emir of Kano , who will deliver the Flagship Keynote, “People, Planet & Prosperity: The Decade of Delivery.” The gathering will also feature H.E. Dr. Kadri Obafemi Hamzat, Deputy Governor of Lagos State; Akintunde Oyebode, Commissioner for Finance, Ekiti State and Chairman, Forum of State Commissioners of Finance; H.E. Amb. Prof. (Mrs.) Olufolake AbdulRazaq, First Lady of Kwara State; Tenioye Majekodunmi, Director-General, National Council on Climate Change; Dr. Innocent Barikor, Director-General/CEO, NESREA; Rukaiya El-Rufai, Presidency / National Economic Council & Climate Change; Adam Boros, Vice President, Africa Finance Corporation; Ademola Ogunbanjo, President & CEO, Oando Clean Energy; Rolake Akinkugbe-Filani, CEO, EnergyInc Advisors Limited; and Dapo Otunla, Chief Corporate Services Officer, IHS Nigeria, among other leaders. The current programme also features a high-level dialogue on mobilizing capital and leadership for Africa’s sustainability transition. First convened in 2016, STS has spent a decade bringing together stakeholders around the green economy, climate finance, technology, circularity, food security, ESG and the Sustainable Development Goals. STS @10 marks an inflection point: a greater focus on bridging Africa’s sustainability implementation gap—the distance between commitments and action, innovation and scale, and viable projects and the investment required to deliver them. “Africa does not suffer from a shortage of ambition, declarations or conferences. The real deficit is execution—turning policy into implementation, innovation into scale and credible projects into investible opportunities,” said Kayode Olaniyan , Convener of the Sustainability Table Discourse Series. “Ten years of STS have shown us the power of bringing the right people to the table. But the next decade must be about what happens after they leave it. We are not convening another talk shop. The next decade must be aboutdelivery,” He added. The programme will focus on four critical conversations: Nigeria’s energy future and expanding energy access; Technology, AI and the SDGs; the circular economy and responsible production; and resilient food systems, smarter value chains and cold-chain infrastructure. The current programme also features a high-level dialogue on mobilizing capital and leadership for Africa’s sustainability transition. First convened in 2016, STS has spent a decade bringing together stakeholders around the green economy, climate finance, technology, circularity, food security, ESG and the Sustainable Development Goals. STS @10 marks an inflection point: a greater focus on bridging Africa’s sustainability implementation gap—the distance between commitments and action, innovation and scale, and viable projects and the investment required to deliver them. “Africa does not suffer from a shortage of ambition, declarations or conferences. But the next decade must be about what happens after they leave it. We are not convening another talk shop. The next decade must be aboutdelivery,” He added. The programme will focus on four critical conversations: Nigeria’s energy future and expanding energy access; Technology, AI and the SDGs; the circular economy and responsible production; and resilient food systems, smarter value chains and cold-chain infrastructure. Beyond the conversations, STS @10 will move from ideas to investment and innovation. Day Two will feature masterclasses, strategic investment engagements, the STS @10 Investment & Deals Room — Connecting Capital with Projects and Enterprise, and an Innovation Pitch Finale & Investor Showcase, creating opportunities to connect promising businesses and projects with financial institutions, investors and development partners. The anniversary will also feature ‘The Earth Speaks’ Sustainability & Arts Exhibition, the launch of the commemorative coffee-table book A Decade at the Table: From Conversation to Transformation, and the premiere of the documentary Nigeria 2030: The Sustainability Imperative — A Decade of Dialogue. A New Era of Action. The gala programme confirms both the book launch and documentary premiere as part of the anniversary celebrations. Ten years ago, STS created a table for the conversation. At STS @10, the question is no longer simply who is at the table—but what gets done because they were there. item.title: The great Halley's Comet disappointment of 1986 — and the discoveries that changed astronomy forever
item.description: null This year, 2026, marks the 40th anniversary of the most recent appearance of Halley's Comet, the most famous comet in the solar system. Roughly every 76 years, Halley punctuates history like an exclamation mark in the night sky. As writer Guy Ottewell has said, it is the "wildest of the tame comets." It is a tame comet because it can be anticipated. It is wild because it is still fresh and bright; the brightest of all the recurring comets. It is the only one that periodically becomes conspicuous to the naked eye. Halley through history Before 1986, Halley had been seen and recorded on 29 occasions. In A.D. 66, observers described it as a sword in the skies above Jerusalem. In 1066, its image was woven into the strip of linen now known as the Bayeux Tapestry , where an agitated crowd of Saxons points toward a fiery comet we know to be Halley. In 1301, the Florentine painter Giotto di Bondone witnessed the comet and was so impressed that, a few years later, he depicted a comet as the star that led the Magi to Bethlehem in one of his magnificent frescoes in Padua's Scrovegni Chapel . More recently, Halley passed unusually close to Earth in 1910. As the 1986 return approached, people who remembered that earlier appearance likely told their children and grandchildren about being awakened before dawn and taken outside to see a huge, ghostly, gleaming object in the sky. Halley's earlier appearances suggested that each return to the inner solar system might produce a magnificent display. Little wonder, then, that the public expected great things in 1986. Vintage engraving A fiery star appears in England, portentous of disaster and is apostrophized by the Monk of Malmesbury. (Image credit: Getty Images) The great disappointment of 1986 Halley's 1986 return therefore became two very different stories: a frustrating spectacle for much of the public and an unprecedented scientific opportunity for astronomers. But for many who saw it — or tried to — in 1986, Halley is remembered as a tremendous disappointment. Heavily promoted as the most anticipated celestial event of the second half of the 20th century, the comet proved to be an underwhelming sight that belied promises of a spectacle never to be seen again. Halley's Comet captured from the Ford Observatory in 1986. (Image credit: Bettmann / Contributor via Getty Images) In all fairness, Halley's subpar performance was not unexpected. During the mid-1970's, comet experts had warned that the comet would likely disappoint much of the general public. Halley logos could be found on warm-up jackets, cocktail glasses, cereal boxes, and just about everything in sight. item.content:encoded: null This year, 2026, marks the 40th anniversary of the most recent appearance of Halley's Comet, the most famous comet in the solar system. Roughly every 76 years, Halley punctuates history like an exclamation mark in the night sky. As writer Guy Ottewell has said, it is the "wildest of the tame comets." It is a tame comet because it can be anticipated. It is wild because it is still fresh and bright; the brightest of all the recurring comets. It is the only one that periodically becomes conspicuous to the naked eye. Halley through history Before 1986, Halley had been seen and recorded on 29 occasions. In A.D. 66, observers described it as a sword in the skies above Jerusalem. In 1066, its image was woven into the strip of linen now known as the Bayeux Tapestry , where an agitated crowd of Saxons points toward a fiery comet we know to be Halley. In 1301, the Florentine painter Giotto di Bondone witnessed the comet and was so impressed that, a few years later, he depicted a comet as the star that led the Magi to Bethlehem in one of his magnificent frescoes in Padua's Scrovegni Chapel . More recently, Halley passed unusually close to Earth in 1910. As the 1986 return approached, people who remembered that earlier appearance likely told their children and grandchildren about being awakened before dawn and taken outside to see a huge, ghostly, gleaming object in the sky. Halley's earlier appearances suggested that each return to the inner solar system might produce a magnificent display. Little wonder, then, that the public expected great things in 1986. Vintage engraving A fiery star appears in England, portentous of disaster and is apostrophized by the Monk of Malmesbury. (Image credit: Getty Images) The great disappointment of 1986 Halley's 1986 return therefore became two very different stories: a frustrating spectacle for much of the public and an unprecedented scientific opportunity for astronomers. But for many who saw it — or tried to — in 1986, Halley is remembered as a tremendous disappointment. Heavily promoted as the most anticipated celestial event of the second half of the 20th century, the comet proved to be an underwhelming sight that belied promises of a spectacle never to be seen again. Halley's Comet captured from the Ford Observatory in 1986. (Image credit: Bettmann / Contributor via Getty Images) In all fairness, Halley's subpar performance was not unexpected. During the mid-1970's, comet experts had warned that the comet would likely disappoint much of the general public. Despite that, the comet's impending arrival was accompanied by a frenzy of T-shirts, commemorative comet medals, bumper stickers, and specially marketed telescopes. Halley logos could be found on warm-up jackets, cocktail glasses, cereal boxes, and just about everything in sight. Caught up in the grip of Halley-mania, the mainstream media emphasized that the comet would be a "once-in-a-lifetime spectacle." One of the main problems for many trying to see the comet that year was light pollution; the total outdoor illumination in the United States had increased tremendously since Halley's previous visit in 1910. Indeed, in 1986, many of the largest cities were bathed in permanent twilight, with only the brightest stars and planets visible from near city centers and with astronomically unacceptable conditions up to 50 miles (80 km) away. On the evening of Jan. 11, in New York City, thousands gathered at four city parks to get a view of Halley's Comet. Mayor Ed Koch and Parks Commissioner Henry J. Stern arranged to have the lights turned off at four public parks, where telescopes were set up. The comet itself was not overly impressive, but many were still happy just to get a glimpse of it. As Stern put it: "Those who came for the comet saw the comet — the cynics didn't — but it was there." When Halley passed through perihelion — its closest point to the sun — on Feb. 9, it lay on the far side of the sun as viewed from Earth and was hidden in the solar glare. During much of March, it brightened only to third magnitude and displayed a tail about a dozen degrees long, merely one-tenth the extent of its 1910 splendor. At the same time, it moved southward through the stars of Sagittarius , Scorpius , and Centaurus . Because those constellations appear low above the southern horizon, the comet was difficult to see from Canada, Europe, and the northern United States. The 1986 apparition was, in fact, described as the comet's worst in 2,000 years. And as one would expect, the public wasn't impressed. Having read that he'd need binoculars and a star map just to find the comet, taxi driver David A. Gittelman penned a New York Times opinion piece entitled " Who Cares About Halley's Comet Anyway?" In it he wrote: "I was devastated. How could such an injustice be allowed to prevail? All my life I'd been waiting — all my life. What happened to the cosmic leviathan of my childhood dreams?" What happened was that at its closest approach to Earth on April 10, Halley was nearly three times farther away than at its minimum distance in 1910. And it had arrived at this point a full two months after perihelion (instead of two weeks as in 1910) — long after its brightest phase had passed. Even those living or traveling to the Southern Hemisphere ( as I did ), where the comet was well placed, didn't witness a true showstopper. To make matters worse, Halley's tail suddenly ebbed at the beginning of April, leaving behind a small, condensed, nebulous mass with a stubby, fan-shaped appendage. The leviathan turned out to be a mere tadpole! A scientific gold mine Reproduction of original plates of Comet Halley 25 May 1910 (Image credit: ESA) But while Halley disappointed the public, it proved to be an astronomical gold mine for astronomers. Within three weeks in March 1986, an international armada of spacecraft studied the comet: Japan launched Sakigake and Suisei ; the Soviet Union sent VEGA 1 and VEGA 2 ; NASA contributed the International Cometary Explorer (ICE); and the European Space Agency, then a consortium of 11 countries, launched Giotto . VEGA 1 and 2 and Giotto plunged deep into Halley's coma — the fuzzy, glowing cloud of gas and dust that surrounds the nucleus when it travels close to the sun — and revealed it to be an active, sputtering mass that responds violently to heating by the sun. Jets of dust were expelled from the nucleus with explosive intensity. And we discovered that the nucleus is encrusted in a dark shroud of its own debris and is as black as coal or velvet. Each VEGA spacecraft came to within about 5,300 miles (8,500 km) of Halley. Giotto passed within just 375 miles (600 km) of the nucleus. More than 2,000 returned images showed that Halley's nucleus was larger than expected and shaped like a peanut or potato, measuring 9 miles (14 km) long and 5 miles (8 km) wide. The nucleus spins on its longest axis every 7.4 days, while the entire body appears to wobble in half that time. The images also revealed three "active regions," areas where volatile gases and dust escape when sunlight heats the surface. As the comet rotates, fresh ice enters the sunlight and sublimates ; the escaping gas then drags entrained dust particles away from the nucleus. item.title: From Asake’s Oba to Omah Lay’s Canada Breeze: 5 Music Videos to Watch
item.description: On set for his Oba music video, Asake highlights his signature high-steeze look with a textured jacket and luxury travel accessories. Music is a daily business in Nigeria, both for the artists making it and the listeners who keep up with new releases. Almost every week, new songs drop alongside music videos that bring them to life visually. This week, we’re putting you on five new music videos to check out, featuring Asake , Omah Lay , FOLA , and Young Jonn . Here are five new Nigerian music videos that are worth adding to your watch list this week: Asake – Oba Asake takes fans into the creative process behind “Oba,” trading elaborate street scenes for a more intimate look at a late-night recording session. Directed by Director Buise, the video features the singer alongside producers and backing vocalists, while his signature style and confident presence reinforce the royal theme of the song. The track appears on his M$NEY album. Omah Lay – Canada Breeze Omah Lay’s “Canada Breeze” captures the singer’s reflective side, touching on personal growth, spirituality and finding peace after periods of worry. The song, from his Clarity of Mind album, pairs his signature melodic delivery with lyrics about moving beyond past struggles. Its music video gives fans another way to experience the record’s introspective mood. FOLA – miss you ii FOLA returns to matters of the heart with “miss you ii (nriri),” a release that speaks to longing and missing someone. The track features the Nigerian singer’s melodic Afropop style and arrives as part of a busy period for the rising artist, whose 9 album was released in October 2026. Fans can check out the song’s lyric video and follow its story through the lyrics. Omah Lay – Artificial Happiness Omah Lay takes a cinematic approach to “Artificial Happiness,” the opening track of his Clarity of Mind album. In the video, the singer awakens in an abandoned warehouse with a white tree at its centre, surrounded by mysterious figures whose movements give the scene an unsettling quality. Co-directed creatively by Omah Lay and his longtime collaborator NWSPK, the visual explores the song’s introspective world and the search for genuine happiness. Young Jonn – Glass in the Air Young Jonn brings dancefloor energy to “Glass in the Air.” The song reflects the excitement of navigating new territory and celebrating personal milestones, with the producer-turned-singer leaning into an upbeat, dance-ready sound. It is another opportunity to experience the infectious energy and melodic style that have become central to his evolution as an artist. The post From Asake’s Oba to Omah Lay’s Canada Breeze: 5 Music Videos to Watch appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. Read today! .

Young Jonn – Glass in the Air Young Jonn brings dancefloor energy to “Glass in the Air.” The song reflects the excitement of navigating new territory and celebrating personal milestones, with the producer-turned-singer leaning into an upbeat, dance-ready sound. It is another opportunity to experience the infectious energy and melodic style that have become central to his evolution as an artist. item.title: A faint glow from the early universe could help solve the mystery of dark energy
item.description: null Hydrogen may be the most common element in the cosmos, but scientists could use it to do something unique: uncover the nature of dark energy, the mysterious force driving the accelerating expansion of the universe. This new line of dark energy investigation comes from the fact that researchers have determined that the CHIME (Canadian Hydrogen Intensity Mapping Experiment) project can detect the faint radio glow of hydrogen from the universe's distant past. Not only does this represent a faster and much less expensive way to investigate dark energy, but it is a major milestone for CHIME. The instrument was specifically devised to investigate dark energy and its pervasive influence. "This is a completely new technique for probing the cosmos, delivered by an instrument that was conceived and built by Canadians," CHIME principal investigator Mark Halpern of the University of British Columbia said in a statement . "It's a bold new step in the global cosmology program and a Canadian success story." Why is dark energy so problematic? Dark energy is the mysterious force that is accelerating the expansion of the universe . It is so problematic for scientists because it started acting on the fabric of space only after the expansion triggered by the Big Bang had halted. That's akin to pushing a child on a swing, watching it stop, and then seeing the swing start up again without a push. And, not only that, but the swing starts oscillating faster and faster. Consider scientists akin to very worried parents, who would really like to know where this ghostly push came from and how it is going to proceed. Just as, if the push on the swing continues, the child could end up in the bushes, or in orbit, the strengthening of dark energy could result in the cold death of the cosmos, or even a " Big Rip " scenario that sees space shredded. Alternatively, if it weakens and allows gravity to reassert dominance, then the universe could collapse back in on itself, resulting in a " Big Crunch " ending that sees the cosmos compressed back into a singularity, as it was at the beginning of time. Dark energy is now the dominant element of the universe, accounting for 68% of the universe's matter-energy budget. It's little wonder that scientists are very keen to know what this mysterious force is. The universe's matter-energy budget showing the dominance of dark energy (Image credit: Robert Lea (created with Canva)) So how can hydrogen help the investigation of dark energy? "Hydrogen is the most common element in the universe and the raw material from which stars form," team member Arnab Chakraborty of the University of Toronto said. "Its faint radio emission acts like a cosmic tracer, revealing how matter is distributed across space." Previously, CHIME could map the distribution of hydrogen in the early universe but only by cross-correlating its observations with galaxy survey data from other telescopes, operations that cost millions of dollars and can only focus on regions
item.dc:creator: Robert Lea
item.content:encoded: null Hydrogen may be the most common element in the cosmos, but scientists could use it to do something unique: uncover the nature of dark energy, the mysterious force driving the accelerating expansion of the universe. This new line of dark energy investigation comes from the fact that researchers have determined that the CHIME (Canadian Hydrogen Intensity Mapping Experiment) project can detect the faint radio glow of hydrogen from the universe's distant past. Not only does this represent a faster and much less expensive way to investigate dark energy, but it is a major milestone for CHIME. The instrument was specifically devised to investigate dark energy and its pervasive influence. "This is a completely new technique for probing the cosmos, delivered by an instrument that was conceived and built by Canadians," CHIME principal investigator Mark Halpern of the University of British Columbia said in a statement . "It's a bold new step in the global cosmology program and a Canadian success story." Why is dark energy so problematic? Dark energy is the mysterious force that is accelerating the expansion of the universe . It is so problematic for scientists because it started acting on the fabric of space only after the expansion triggered by the Big Bang had halted. That's akin to pushing a child on a swing, watching it stop, and then seeing the swing start up again without a push. And, not only that, but the swing starts oscillating faster and faster. Consider scientists akin to very worried parents, who would really like to know where this ghostly push came from and how it is going to proceed. Just as, if the push on the swing continues, the child could end up in the bushes, or in orbit, the strengthening of dark energy could result in the cold death of the cosmos, or even a " Big Rip " scenario that sees space shredded. Alternatively, if it weakens and allows gravity to reassert dominance, then the universe could collapse back in on itself, resulting in a " Big Crunch " ending that sees the cosmos compressed back into a singularity, as it was at the beginning of time. Dark energy is now the dominant element of the universe, accounting for 68% of the universe's matter-energy budget. It's little wonder that scientists are very keen to know what this mysterious force is. The universe's matter-energy budget showing the dominance of dark energy (Image credit: Robert Lea (created with Canva)) So how can hydrogen help the investigation of dark energy? "Hydrogen is the most common element in the universe and the raw material from which stars form," team member Arnab Chakraborty of the University of Toronto said. "Its faint radio emission acts like a cosmic tracer, revealing how matter is distributed across space." Previously, CHIME could map the distribution of hydrogen in the early universe but only by cross-correlating its observations with galaxy survey data from other telescopes, operations that cost millions of dollars and can only focus on regions of the universe dense enough to form stars. CHIME has now shown it can map the radio glow of hydrogen all on its own. Indeed, the team has already begun making steps in this direction using just a tiny fraction of existing CHIME data. Using 94 nights of observations from 2019, they detected a hydrogen signal from when the universe was just 5 billion years old. "Our data indicate that roughly 2% of the hydrogen in the universe was in neutral atomic form at this time, broadly consistent with other measurements," team member Shabbir Shaikh of Arizona State University said. "By measuring how that hydrogen is distributed and clustered, CHIME gives us a new way to test our understanding of how galaxies form and evolve." CHIME has now collected seven years of data, and using this, the team is hoping to probe the distribution of hydrogen back to 3 billion years after the Big Bang. The team's research was published across two papers in The Astrophysical Journal .

item.title: 5 Films Bimbo Ademoye and Timini Egbuson Have Featured in Together
item.description: Bimbo Ademoye and Timini Egbuson in western bridal styling for “My 30th Wedding”. If it were rumoured that Bimbo Ademoye and Timini Egbuson are getting married, you’d hardly dismiss the rumour because of the times the duo have shared the stage in films, and their synergy and connection each time they appear together in a film. With their latest YouTube release , “My 30th Wedding” going viral, with over 22 million views in 11 days, it is informative to look at some of the films they have both featured in together. In each film, you will find that connection. While they have mainly featured together in romance movies, the genre has not limited the creativity and energy they bring into each film. Let’s look at some of the films Bimbo Ademoye and Timini Egbuson have both featured in. Breaded Life In this 2021 movie, Bimbo Ademoye and Timini Egbuson navigate life in the ghetto after Timini’s character, Sunmi, is forced out of his wealthy existence. The film showcases the duo’s varying personas, highlighting themes of vulnerability, strength, and love. They demonstrate how two actors can continuously interact on screen while still delivering distinctly different vibes. Reel Love Produced by Timini Egbuson and directed by Kayode Kasum, Reel Love explores the relationship between love, celebrity and social media. Timini plays Tomide Jobi, a relationship influencer whose public image suffers after a heated confrontation with Rachel, played by T.J. Omusuku, goes viral. To repair the damage, Tomide agrees to stage a fake relationship with Rachel, but the arrangement becomes complicated when genuine feelings begin to develop. Bimbo Ademoye appears as Chizaram in the film, which also features Funke Akindele, Shaffy Bello and Dakore Egbuson-Akande. Released in Nigerian cinemas on Valentine’s Day in 2025, the film examines the pressure to maintain a public image and the difference between performing love for an audience and experiencing it in real life. Big Love In Big Love, Bimbo Ademoye and Timini Egbuson play Adina and Adil, two young people who meet while pursuing their ambitions and eventually fall in love. Adil is determined to achieve his dreams, while Adina is an independent woman focused on making a living. As their relationship develops, they must confront personal fears and a secret that threatens to come between them. Directed by Biodun Stephen, the romantic drama explores love, trust and the difficult choices that can test a relationship. The film also gives viewers another opportunity to see the chemistry between the two actors as romantic leads. Unexpected Places Bimbo Ademoye plays Prosper, the daughter of a housekeeper who steps in to manage the household while her mother recovers from surgery. Her new responsibilities bring her into contact with Chris, played by Timini Egbuson, a wealthy playboy whose irresponsible behaviour has become a concern for his father. Her new responsibilities bring her into contact with Chris, played by Timini Egbuson, a wealthy playboy whose irresponsible behaviour has become a concern for his father. Their relationship begins on difficult terms, but Prosper’s presence gradually challenges Chris to reconsider his choices and take responsibility for his life. Produced by Ademoye and directed by Great Val Edochie, the romantic drama explores personal growth, love and the unexpected circumstances that can change people’s lives. The film also takes a more emotional turn as the couple’s relationship develops. Introducing the Kujus Directed by Biodun Stephen, Introducing the Kujus is a family comedy-drama set in Badagry, Lagos. The film follows five siblings who are reluctant to return to their hometown for the fifth anniversary of their mother’s death. Mausi Kuju, played by Bisola Aiyeola, and her brother Maugbe, played by Timini Egbuson, devise a plan to bring the family together, but their complicated relationships threaten to get in the way. Bimbo Ademoye plays Ebi, one of the siblings whose relationships and family history contribute to the story. item.title: Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse review – every fantastical vampire-hunting vision is fulfilled
item.description: Evil Empire/Konami; PC, PS5, Switch, Xbox There are buzzsaws and blood pits, bats burst into blood and demons burn to cinders. The series’ new emphasis on twitch-based action may annoy purists but you can’t call it dull A gorgeously gothic Paris swarming with demons should be a perfect setting for Konami’s long-running vampiric adventure series. Unfortunately, while the sights and sounds of this vivid and haunting world leave a bold impression, developer Evil Empire doesn’t always provide an enjoyable experience to go with them. It takes far too long for the most imaginative elements of the game to be revealed. Players take the role of Rose Belmont, daughter of vampire hunter (and Castlevania regular) Trevor Belmont and the witch Sypha Belnades, and her quest is to free Paris from demonic occupation. This murderous noctural journey feels best when you’re fighting monsters; combat is frenetic, sometimes to the point of being overwhelming, while boss fights require considerable focus and skill. Combat is the game’s strongest component and what sets it apart from previous entries. Minimising the series’ role-playing elements (levelling up has never felt more perfunctory) in favour of twitch-based action will annoy purists, but they’d be hard pressed to call battles dull. Continue reading...

item.title: Midea Launches WIN 9JA WIN Promotion with Guaranteed Rewards and Chery Tiggo 2 Pro Grand Prize
item.description: Midea has announced the launch of WIN 9JA WIN , a nationwide consumer promotion designed to reward Nigerians who choose Midea home appliances during the 2026 festive shopping season. Running from 10 October to 31 December 2026 , the promotion gives every qualifying shopper an instant opportunity to win, with a Chery Tiggo 2 Pro positioned as the ultimate grand prize. Under the promotion, consumers who purchase any Midea product worth ₦100,000 or more from a participating dealer receive a scratch voucher at the point of purchase. The shopper scratches the voucher to reveal the reward won, creating a simple and immediate link between purchase and reward. Every qualifying shopper is a winner, subject to the approved campaign terms and conditions. The campaign combines retail participation with radio, digital, public relations, in-store visibility and an extensive on-ground Promo Tour Truck programme. The touring activation will carry the excitement of WIN 9JA WIN into selected markets and dealer locations, with the Chery Tiggo 2 Pro prominently showcased to give consumers a close view of the campaign’s headline prize. A Consumer Promotion Built Around Instant Reward WIN 9JA WIN is designed to make the festive purchase journey more rewarding while strengthening engagement between Midea , its dealer network and consumers across Nigeria. Its central proposition is straightforward: make a qualifying purchase, receive a scratch voucher and discover the reward immediately. The approved reward pool spans Midea home appliances and branded consumer gifts. These include side-by-side refrigerators, chest freezers, air conditioners, refrigerators, washing machines, air fryers, microwave ovens, kettles, standing fans and blenders, as well as branded T-shirts, caps and pens. The ultimate reward is a Chery Tiggo 2 Pro, presented in the campaign materials as the car to be won. MIDEA NIGERIA | MEDIA RELEASE How Consumers Can Participate Step Consumer action Purchase Buy any Midea product or combination of eligible Midea products worth ₦100,000 or more from a participating dealer between 10 October and 31 December 2026. Receive Collect the campaign scratch voucher issued for the qualifying purchase. Scratch Scratch the voucher to reveal the reward. Claim Follow the verification and prize-claim guidance provided by the participating dealer in accordance with the approved campaign terms and conditions. Additional Midea Air Conditioner Offer Alongside WIN 9JA WIN, Midea is also offering free installation and a free copper kit to consumers who purchase any Midea air conditioner from 1 October through 31 December 2026. The offer extends the campaign’s value beyond the product purchase by helping eligible AC buyers with installation support, subject to the applicable terms and conditions. Promo Tour Truck Takes WIN 9JA WIN Closer to Consumers A major feature of the campaign is the branded Promo Tour Truck programme, developed as a mobile visibility and engagement platform.

The Chery Tiggo 2 Pro will be prominently showcased as part of the tour, allowing shoppers and local communities to see the campaign’s ultimate prize at close range. South-West and South-South route: Ibadan, Iseyin, Ogbomoso, Ilorin, Osogbo, Ilesa, Ile-Ife, Abeokuta, Sagamu, Ijebu-Ode, Ago-Iwoye, Mowe, Warri, Effurun, Ughelli, Sapele, Benin City, Irrua, Uromi, Akure and Ondo. North and North-Central Route: Abuja, Mararaba, Lokoja, Makurdi, Lafia, Kaduna, Kano, Yola and Jimeta. By combining guaranteed rewards with a wide dealer footprint and direct market engagement, WIN 9JA WIN gives consumers another reason to explore Midea’s range of air conditioners, refrigerators, freezers, washing machines, cooking appliances and small domestic appliances during the year-end season. Executive Comment / Quotation “WIN 9JA WIN is our way of thanking Nigerian consumers and making every qualifying purchase more rewarding. The mechanic is simple, transparent and immediate: buy, receive a scratch voucher and reveal your reward. Through the Promo Tour Truck programme, we are also taking the campaign closer to our dealer partners and consumers in markets across the country, while giving shoppers the opportunity to experience Midea products and see the Chery Tiggo 2 Pro grand prize up close.” – Ashok Dimri, Business Head, Africa, of Care Global Consumer Ltd. Call to Action Consumers can visit participating Midea dealers nationwide between 10 October and 31 December 2026, purchase eligible Midea products worth ₦100,000 or more and collect a scratch voucher to reveal their reward. Consumers purchasing any Midea air conditioner can also access the free installation and free copper kit offer through 31 December 2026, subject to the applicable terms and conditions. About Midea Group Midea is one of over 10 brands operating under the Smart Home Business of Midea Group. Midea Group , with the vision of “bringing great innovations to life”, is an international tech-leading company which specializes in seven major business areas: Smart Home, Industrial Technologies, Building Technologies, KUKA, New Energy, Midea Healthcare and ANNTO Logistics. Midea’s products and services have served more than 500 million customers worldwide, including key clients and strategic partners across various industries. Midea operates more than 400 subsidiaries, 41 R&D centres and 65 major manufacturing bases globally, with a business network covering over 200 countries and regions.
